risks.startMessage: `$Digging a fresh grave, your shovel clangs on a rusty strongbox. It is marked "PROPERTY OF THE DEATHVILLE COUNTY MUSEUM".\n\nThe museum closed in 1962. Probably nobody remembers it.
risks.normalMessage: `$You call city hall. The Mayor takes the box, holds a press conference, and somehow never mentions your name. Still, the paper prints a photo of your shovel.
risks.failMessage: `$You pry the box open behind the shed.\n\nInside: a mummified cat and a note reading "WHOEVER OPENS THIS IS CURSED." The cat looks very sure about it. Your luck goes sour by dinner.
risks.successMessage: `$You pry the box open behind the shed.\n\nInside: old silver dollars, a pocket watch, and a perfectly good ham sandwich from 1962. You keep everything but the sandwich. You think about it. You keep the sandwich too.

risks.startMessage: `$A rival's hearse is parked outside the Pale Horse Cafe with the engine running. The driver is inside ordering pie.\n\nThe body in the back is headed for a funeral across town. It could just as easily be headed for *PARLOR*.
risks.normalMessage: `$You walk on by. Stealing a corpse in broad daylight is beneath you. You'd at least wait until dusk.
risks.failMessage: `$You hop in and floor it.\n\nTwo blocks later you realize the hearse has a GPS tracker, a dashcam, and the driver's mother in the passenger seat. She hits you with her purse the whole way to the police station.
risks.successMessage: `$You hop in and floor it.\n\nBy the time the driver finishes his pie, the deceased is resting comfortably in your slumber room and the family is signing your paperwork. Nobody asks why the hearse is a different color.

risks.startMessage: `$The embalming pump makes a noise like a goose being stepped on and quits.\n\nYou have a viewing at four. The manual says "DO NOT OPERATE BY HAND." It does not say why.
risks.normalMessage: `$You call the repairman. He arrives in twenty minutes, charges you double, and lectures you about filters. The viewing goes off without a hitch.
risks.failMessage: `$You roll up your sleeves and start pumping by hand.\n\nNow you know why. The hose comes loose and the embalming room gets a fresh coat of pink. So do you. So does the family, who came early.
risks.successMessage: `$You roll up your sleeves and start pumping by hand.\n\nIt takes three hours and your forearms are now enormous, but the body looks great. The repairman's bill stays in his pocket.

risks.startMessage: `$Father Smyth leaves the collection plate from the bake sale on your counter while he goes to find his car keys.\n\nThere is over two hundred dollars in it. And a lemon bar.
risks.normalMessage: `$You stand guard over the plate like a soldier. Father Smyth returns and blesses you for your honesty. He also takes the lemon bar back, which seems unnecessary.
risks.failMessage:
`$You slip a few bills into your pocket.

`wFather Smyth: `$"I counted it before I left, my child."

He makes you put it back, plus interest, plus a donation, plus you're running the ring toss at the next carnival.
risks.successMessage: `$You slip a few bills into your pocket.\n\nFather Smyth comes back, picks up the plate and says "The Lord provides." He's right. The Lord just provided for you.

risks.startMessage: `$A crate arrives from Di-Mart addressed to a rival parlor. It's a brand new Gold casket, delivered to you by mistake.\n\nElijah's delivery boy, who is 64, is already driving away.
risks.normalMessage: `$You call Di-Mart and they send the boy back for it. It takes him most of the afternoon. Elijah thanks you without blinking, which is how he does everything.
risks.failMessage: `$You drag it into the storeroom and slap your own price tag on it.\n\nThat night Elijah appears in your window. He does not knock. He does not blink. You have no idea how long he's been standing there. You pay for the casket.
risks.successMessage: `$You drag it into the storeroom and slap your own price tag on it.\n\nThe rival blames Di-Mart, Di-Mart blames the boy, and the boy blames his hip. You sell the casket by lunch.

risks.startMessage: `$A grieving widow asks if you can play her husband's favorite song at the service. She hands you a cassette labeled "HAROLD - DO NOT ERASE".\n\nYou don't have a cassette player. You do have a kazoo.
risks.normalMessage: `$You drive to Di-Mart and buy a tape deck at the emergency price. The song plays. Harold's widow weeps. It's polka, but she weeps.
risks.failMessage: `$At the service you perform the song by ear on kazoo.\n\nYou don't know the song. You play something you heard in an elevator. The widow stands up in the middle of the second verse and leaves the chapel. So does everyone else.
risks.successMessage: `$At the service you perform the song by ear on kazoo.\n\nIt is so bad it loops back around to beautiful. People are still talking about it at the reception. Two families book you on the spot.

risks.startMessage: `$The Nurse calls from the hospital.\n\n`wNurse: `$"Hi prince! Somebody left a body down here with no toe tag. First parlor to sign for it gets it. Want me to put your name down? Nobody would know if, you know, the paperwork got creative."
risks.normalMessage:
`w*NAME*: `$"Let's do it properly. Find the family first."

`wNurse: `$"Oh, you're no fun. But you're honest-no-fun, and that's the best kind."

She sends you a referral anyway.
risks.failMessage: `w*NAME*: `$"Put me down. Say it's my uncle."\n\nThe body turns out to be the Mayor's brother-in-law. He was not your uncle. The Mayor would like a word, and the word is "audit".
risks.successMessage: `w*NAME*: `$"Put me down. Say it's my uncle."\n\nUncle Mystery gets a lovely service. The family turns up a week later, sees how nice it was, and pays the whole bill without asking questions.

risks.startMessage: `$Morty the skeleton has fallen off his hook and lost a finger bone down the floor drain.\n\nYou could fish it out. Or you could borrow one from a client. They're not using it.
risks.normalMessage: `$You spend an hour with a coat hanger and a flashlight and get Morty's finger back. He seems grateful. It's hard to tell. It's always hard to tell with Morty.
risks.failMessage: `$You borrow a finger from the gentleman in the cold room.\n\nAt his open-casket viewing, his daughter counts. Out loud. Up to nine.
risks.successMessage: `$You borrow a finger from the gentleman in the cold room.\n\nMorty looks complete again, and the gentleman is buried in gloves. Nobody counts. Nobody ever counts.

risks.startMessage: `$The Twins are leaning on your mailbox, sharing a single cigarette.\n\n`wThe Twins: `y"We could make that new parlor across town have a really warm evening. For you, a discount. Half price. We just like the work."
risks.normalMessage: `$You tell the Twins to get off your property. They leave together, in step, without looking back. It is the creepiest thing you have seen all week, and you work with corpses.
risks.failMessage: `$You shake both their hands, one after the other.\n\nThe Twins are very thorough. They burn down the wrong parlor. It is yours. They send you a bill.
risks.successMessage: `$You shake both their hands, one after the other.\n\nThat night the sky across town glows orange. The next morning the rival's families are lined up outside *PARLOR*, smelling faintly of smoke.

risks.startMessage: `$A man in a very nice suit asks if you could cremate "a few boxes of old paperwork" along with his late business partner.\n\nThe boxes are labeled EVIDENCE. He offers cash.
risks.normalMessage: `$You politely decline. He politely leaves. You politely call the police, who politely thank you and buy a pre-need plan on the way out.
risks.failMessage: `$You toss the boxes in with the partner.\n\nThe smoke from your chimney spells out, very faintly, "TAX FRAUD". The fire department comes. Then the police. Then three men from the state who do not smile.
risks.successMessage: `$You toss the boxes in with the partner.\n\nThe cash is crisp, the partner burns evenly, and the man in the suit leaves you a business card that just says "WE'LL BE IN TOUCH". Hopefully that's good.

risks.startMessage: `$The Teller at the bank counts your deposit twice, frowns, and slides it back.\n\n`wTeller: `$"There's an extra five hundred here, *SIR*. Someone else's envelope must have gotten mixed in with yours. Would you like to... look again?"
risks.normalMessage:
`w*NAME*: `$"That's not mine."

`wTeller: `$"How refreshing. I'll make a note that you can count."

The Teller almost smiles. The rightful owner sends you a thank-you fruit basket.
risks.failMessage:
`w*NAME*: `$"Oh, that's definitely mine. I earned it."

`wTeller: `$"Interesting, since it's in an envelope that says ORPHANAGE."

The Teller closes the window in your face, slowly, and you have to stand in line again to pay it back.
risks.successMessage:
`w*NAME*: `$"Oh, that's definitely mine. I earned it."

`wTeller: `$"Very well. I'm sure you did."

She doesn't believe you. But she doesn't do paperwork after four, either.

risks.startMessage: `$Old Man Withers falls asleep in your showroom, sitting up in a Silver casket.\n\nHe's breathing. Probably. A family is coming in at noon to pick out a casket and he's in the nicest one.
risks.normalMessage: `$You gently wake him. He accuses you of trying to bury him alive, buys nothing, eats three of your mints and leaves. Still, he tells everyone at bingo you've got comfy caskets.
risks.failMessage: `$You fold his hands on his chest and tell the family he's "a display model".\n\nHalfway through your pitch Withers sits bolt upright and shouts "BINGO!" The mother faints. The father takes his business, and his wife, to Blaine.
risks.successMessage: `$You fold his hands on his chest and tell the family he's "a display model".\n\nThey are so impressed by how peaceful he looks that they buy the Silver on the spot, then a second one for Grandma. Withers sleeps through the whole sale.

risks.startMessage: `$A wreath arrives for the Pickett funeral. The card reads "With deepest sympathy, from *PARLOR*."\n\nYou didn't send it. A rival did, and spelled your name on it by mistake. You could just leave it there.
risks.normalMessage: `$You call the florist and have the card corrected. It hurts. It hurts a lot. But your conscience is clean, which is more than you can say for your hearse.
risks.failMessage: `$You leave the card and accept the family's thanks with a solemn nod.\n\nThen the rival shows up at the service with the receipt. He reads it out loud, slowly, during the eulogy.
risks.successMessage: `$You leave the card and accept the family's thanks with a solemn nod.\n\nThe Picketts are so touched they send all their remaining relatives your way. There are a lot of Picketts. They die a lot.

risks.startMessage: `$The town's water main has burst and the old section of your graveyard is a lake. Two caskets are floating toward the road.\n\nYou could fish them back. Or you could call them "a new water feature" and charge admission.
risks.normalMessage: `$You wade in up to your armpits and tow the caskets home with a rope. The families never find out. You find out what was in the water, and you shower for a week.
risks.failMessage: `$You put up a sign: "LAKE OF THE DEAD - $2".\n\nThe first paying customer is the Deathville Enquirer. The second is the health inspector. The third is a lawyer, floating past on a casket lid.
risks.successMessage: `$You put up a sign: "LAKE OF THE DEAD - $2".\n\nBy noon there is a line around the block, a hot dog cart, and a couple getting engaged on a floating headstone. You've never made more money from the dead without burying anyone.

risks.startMessage: `$You're out of burial suits. The deceased is a large man and the only thing his size in the building is your own good suit, the one you wear to conventions.\n\nOr there's the curtain.
risks.normalMessage: `$You dress him in your good suit. He looks better in it than you ever did. You'll miss that suit. The family won't stop thanking you.
risks.failMessage: `$You stitch together a quick suit from the showroom curtains.\n\nThe pattern is very loud. At the viewing, a woman asks why her uncle is wearing her old living room. It was her old living room. You bought the curtains at her yard sale.
risks.successMessage: `$You stitch together a quick suit from the showroom curtains.\n\nVelvet, tassels, the works. The family thinks it's a designer piece and asks where they can get one. You take three orders.

risks.startMessage:
`$A drunk wanders into the showroom at closing time and lies down in your cheapest Wood casket.

`wDrunk: `$"Jus' five minutes... I'll pay ya..."

He has a very full wallet sticking out of his back pocket.
risks.normalMessage: `$You call him a cab and pour him into it. The next day he comes back, embarrassed, and pre-pays for a funeral. "Same box," he says. "It was comfy."
risks.failMessage: `$You close the lid and start a meter.\n\nAt two in the morning he wakes up in the dark, in a box, and screams for an hour. The neighbors call the police, the police call the paper, and the paper calls you "THE COFFIN MOTEL".
risks.successMessage: `$You close the lid and start a meter.\n\nIn the morning he climbs out refreshed, pays the overnight rate plus breakfast, and tells all his friends. You may have invented something.

risks.startMessage: `$During a viewing, the deceased's toupee slides off and lands in the punch bowl.\n\nNobody has noticed yet. You could fish it out in front of everyone, or you could quietly move the punch bowl into the back.
risks.normalMessage: `$You fish the toupee out with the ladle, wring it into a napkin, and put it back on with dignity. Somebody claps. It's a sincere clap.
risks.failMessage: `$You lift the bowl and casually walk toward the kitchen.\n\nThe widow stops you to get a refill. She ladles out the toupee. She holds it up. She looks at her husband. She looks at you.
risks.successMessage: `$You lift the bowl and casually walk toward the kitchen.\n\nYou swap it for a fresh one and nobody suspects a thing. The deceased spends eternity with a hat on, and the family thinks it was his wish.

risks.startMessage: `$You find a spare key to a rival's parlor on the sidewalk. The tag says "BACK DOOR".\n\nTheir big funeral is tomorrow. You could just go and have a look around. A long look. With a screwdriver.
risks.normalMessage: `$You return the key. The rival is so stunned by your decency that he gives you a box of donuts and a hearse air freshener. It's a good air freshener.
risks.failMessage: `$You let yourself in at midnight and loosen every casket hinge in the building.\n\nThe rival is waiting in the dark with a flashlight, a camera and a very large dog. You are on the front page in your pajamas.
risks.successMessage: `$You let yourself in at midnight and loosen every casket hinge in the building.\n\nAt tomorrow's big funeral the lid flops off during the eulogy. The family walks straight across the street to *PARLOR*.

risks.startMessage: `$Mr. Yang delivers lunch himself and leaves his delivery bag on your counter while he uses the restroom.\n\nInside are four more orders, and a whole stack of fortune cookies. One of them could have your name on it. Literally, if you had a pen.
risks.normalMessage: `$You leave the bag alone. Mr. Yang comes back, notices, and gives you an extra egg roll. "You are a good customer," he says. "Too pale. But good."
risks.failMessage: `$You slip a fortune into a rival's cookie: "YOUR PARLOR SMELLS. EVERYONE SAYS SO."\n\nJune recognizes your handwriting from the tip line on your receipts. Yang's bans you for a week and tapes your photo to the register.
risks.successMessage: `$You slip a fortune into a rival's cookie: "YOUR PARLOR SMELLS. EVERYONE SAYS SO."\n\nThe rival reads it out loud at the Pale Horse Cafe. Everyone agrees. He spends the next day scrubbing instead of selling.

risks.startMessage: `$A family wants their grandfather buried with his old war medals. They look very real and very valuable. The family is in a hurry and won't be checking the casket.
risks.normalMessage: `$You pin the medals on his chest and salute. It feels good, actually. You'd forgotten what that felt like.
risks.failMessage: `$You swap the medals for bottle caps painted gold and take the real ones to a collector.\n\nThe collector is grandpa's old army buddy. He is very old and very strong, and he wants a word in the parking lot.
risks.successMessage: `$You swap the medals for bottle caps painted gold and take the real ones to a collector.\n\nGrandpa goes to his rest looking very decorated in the dim light. The collector pays cash. You try not to think about it.

risks.startMessage: `$The county inspector is on his way for the yearly check of the embalming room. The drain is clogged with something you'd rather not name.\n\nYou could fix it, or you could put a rug over it.
risks.normalMessage: `$You snake the drain. What comes out will haunt you, but the inspector gives you a passing grade and a lollipop. He gives everyone a lollipop.
risks.failMessage: `$You throw a nice rug over the drain and stand on it, smiling.\n\nThe inspector asks you to step aside. The rug gurgles. He writes for a long time, then asks for a second clipboard.
risks.successMessage: `$You throw a nice rug over the drain and stand on it, smiling.\n\nThe inspector compliments the rug, signs the form, and leaves. The rug is ruined, but rugs are cheaper than fines.

risks.startMessage: `$A teenager offers to film your next funeral for his online video channel.\n\n`wTeen: `$"It'll go totally viral, dude. People love sad stuff. Do I get to touch the body?"
risks.normalMessage: `$You tell him funerals are private. He calls you "a total grandpa" and leaves. The family is grateful. Grandpas, it turns out, are good for business.
risks.failMessage: `$You let him film.\n\nThe video goes viral, all right. It's called "FUNERAL GUY TRIPS INTO GRAVE (NOT CLICKBAIT)". Three million people watch you fall in. Nobody in Deathville will make eye contact.
risks.successMessage: `$You let him film.\n\nThe video, "MOST BEAUTIFUL FUNERAL EVER?? (CRYING)", gets a million views. People drive in from Blaine just to die near your parlor. Some of them manage it.

risks.startMessage: `$A scruffy man in a lab coat knocks on your back door at midnight.\n\n`wCousin Sal: `$"Hey, buddy. Got a guy here. Paperwork's coming. Probably. Can you hold him in your cold room for a couple days? I'll make it worth your while."
risks.normalMessage: `$You close the door on Cousin Sal. Through the wood you hear him say "your loss, buddy" and then the sound of a station wagon refusing to start. You sleep like a baby.
risks.failMessage: `$You wheel the guy into the cold room and take Sal's cash.\n\nThe guy is the missing bank robber from the Deathville Enquirer. The police find him behind your ice cream. They also find the ice cream.
risks.successMessage: `$You wheel the guy into the cold room and take Sal's cash.\n\nTwo days later Sal comes back with the paperwork, which is mostly legible. You do the service. Sal pays you twice by mistake.

risks.startMessage: `$Lightning strikes the big oak in your graveyard and splits it right down the middle.\n\nUnder the roots is a coffin with no headstone and no record. Its lid has a little brass plate that says only "RICH".
risks.normalMessage: `$You rebury the coffin, plant a sapling and say a few words. Father Smyth hears about it and mentions you in Sunday's sermon under "people who did not open the coffin".
risks.failMessage: `$You pry open the lid.\n\nInside is Mr. Rich, who was a magician. His last trick is a spring-loaded snake, a cloud of purple powder and an air horn. Your hair is purple for a month.
risks.successMessage: `$You pry open the lid.\n\nMr. Rich was, it turns out, rich. Gold teeth, gold cufflinks and a gold-plated harmonica. You play one song on it in his honor, then sell it.

risks.startMessage: `$A woman pays in full for her husband's funeral and leaves. Ten minutes later you realize she paid twice: once by check and once in cash.\n\nShe left her phone number. In very large handwriting.
risks.normalMessage: `$You call and refund the cash. She is so grateful she cries on the phone, then tells her entire book club. The book club is mostly widows. Book clubs are always mostly widows.
risks.failMessage: `$You pocket the cash and lose the phone number.\n\nShe comes back for her reading glasses and sees her own twenties in your tip jar. She knows they're hers. She writes her initials on all of them.
risks.successMessage: `$You pocket the cash and lose the phone number.\n\nShe never notices. She was very rich and very sad and is now in Florida. You buy a better coffee maker in her honor.

risks.startMessage:
`$Elijah offers you a pallet of "slightly used" caskets at a fraction of the wholesale price.

`wElijah: `$"No questions about where they came from. And I mean that as a rule, not a suggestion."

He does not blink while he says it.
risks.normalMessage: `$You pass. Elijah stares at you for a full minute, then writes something in a little black book. You decide not to ask what.
risks.failMessage: `$You buy the pallet.\n\nThe first one you sell still has a name engraved inside the lid. The name belongs to the customer's grandmother. She was buried last spring. In Blaine. In that casket.
risks.successMessage: `$You buy the pallet.\n\nA little sanding, a little polish, a new satin lining. Good as new. Nobody needs to know they're on their second tour of duty.

risks.startMessage: `$The Mayor's portrait at city hall is being painted, and he wants a "dramatic graveyard background".\n\nHe's offered to pose among your headstones. He'd like it if one of the headstones had his name on it, "for gravitas".
risks.normalMessage: `$You let him pose among the real headstones. He grumbles, but the painting comes out moody and grand, and it hangs in city hall with a little plaque thanking *PARLOR*.
risks.failMessage: `$You carve a quick headstone with the Mayor's name and today's date.\n\nThe local paper runs the photo without the caption. Half the town thinks the Mayor is dead. The other half is disappointed when they find out he isn't. He blames you for both halves.
risks.successMessage: `$You carve a quick headstone with the Mayor's name and today's date.\n\nThe Mayor loves it so much he buys it, and a plot to go under it, and the plot next to it "for the dog".

risks.startMessage: `$Two families have booked the chapel for the same time. Both are paying full price. Both have already sent the invitations.\n\nYou could cancel one, or you could try to do both funerals at once and hope nobody notices.
risks.normalMessage: `$You call the second family, apologize, and move them to tomorrow with a free floral arrangement. They're disappointed but impressed. Mostly impressed by the flowers.
risks.failMessage: `$You put a curtain down the middle of the chapel and run back and forth.\n\nYou get the names mixed up in both eulogies. Two widows meet behind the curtain and compare notes. They compare them loudly.
risks.successMessage: `$You put a curtain down the middle of the chapel and run back and forth.\n\nBoth families think you gave them your full attention. You've never sweated so much in a suit, and you've never been paid so well for it.

risks.startMessage: `$Your hearse needs new tires before tomorrow's procession. The tire shop is closed. A rival's hearse is parked next door with four beautiful new ones.\n\nYou have a jack.
risks.normalMessage: `$You drive the procession at eight miles an hour on your bald tires. The mourners think it's a mark of respect. You let them.
risks.failMessage: `$You swap all four tires in the dark.\n\nThe rival's security light comes on halfway through. He watches from his window, eating cereal, then calls the police, then calls the Enquirer, then calls his mother, for some reason.
risks.successMessage: `$You swap all four tires in the dark.\n\nThe next morning your hearse glides through town like a swan. The rival's hearse sits on blocks. He doesn't make it to the cemetery. You do.

risks.startMessage: `$A man in a tracksuit wants to rent a casket "for a magic trick" at a birthday party.\n\n`wMan: `$"I lie in it, they nail it shut, I escape. It's my big finish. I've done it twice. Well, once."
risks.normalMessage: `$You explain that caskets are for the dead and not for party tricks. He leaves sulking. A week later he comes back to buy one for real, for his manager.
risks.failMessage: `$You rent him your best Silver.\n\nHe does not escape. The party guests clap for twenty minutes before anyone gets a crowbar. He's fine, but the casket is not, and he wants a refund.
risks.successMessage: `$You rent him your best Silver.\n\nHe escapes in a puff of smoke to wild applause. He returns the casket the next day, a bit scratched, with a tip and a coupon for a free balloon animal.

risks.startMessage: `$Your Forever Fragrant air freshener order hasn't come and today's viewing is a man who's been in a hot attic for a while.\n\nThere is a can of bug spray, a bottle of vanilla extract, and half a pizza.
risks.normalMessage: `$You call the family and postpone the viewing until the order arrives. They're grateful. Nobody wants that kind of memory, even of someone they didn't like.
risks.failMessage: `$You mix the bug spray and the vanilla into a fine mist and fill the room with it.\n\nThe mourners now smell like cookies and poison. One of them sneezes on the body. The whole room starts sneezing. You can't stop sneezing. It's on the news.
risks.successMessage: `$You mix the bug spray and the vanilla into a fine mist and fill the room with it.\n\nThe mourners say the room smells "like Grandma's house". The family asks for the recipe. You decide to bottle it.

risks.startMessage: `$A pigeon has flown into the chapel and is perched on the casket during a service. The family thinks it's the spirit of their dear departed.\n\nYou know it's just a pigeon. It's the same pigeon from last week.
risks.normalMessage: `$You open a window and politely wave the pigeon outside. The family is a little sad, but you've saved them from what pigeons inevitably do next.
risks.failMessage: `$You announce, in your most solemn voice, that the spirit has come to say goodbye.\n\nThe spirit poops on the widow. Then on the urn. Then on Father Smyth. Father Smyth says "this can't be good" and goes home.
risks.successMessage: `$You announce, in your most solemn voice, that the spirit has come to say goodbye.\n\nThe pigeon coos, flaps once and flies away right on cue. There isn't a dry eye in the house. The family pays extra for "the bird service".

risks.startMessage: `$At the Spirit University library you find an old thesis titled "Upselling the Bereaved Through Hypnosis". The library computer is busy, so nobody is watching.\n\nThe chapter on swinging a pocket watch looks promising.
risks.normalMessage: `$You put the thesis back on the shelf. Some things are too evil even for the funeral business. You check out a book on bereavement counseling instead. It's surprisingly useful.
risks.failMessage: `$You swing your pocket watch in front of the next customer and murmur "gold casket... gold casket..."\n\nHe hypnotizes you instead. You wake up an hour later having bought his car.
risks.successMessage: `$You swing your pocket watch in front of the next customer and murmur "gold casket... gold casket..."\n\nShe buys the gold casket, the plot, a statue and a ferret. You don't sell ferrets. You'll figure that out later.

risks.startMessage: `$Inspector Mudge has left his clipboard on your counter while he inspects the basement.\n\nYour name is on the top sheet. Most of the boxes say FAIL. A pencil with a good eraser is lying right next to it.
risks.normalMessage: `$You leave the clipboard alone. Mudge comes back up, reads his own notes and sighs. "Honest, at least," he writes at the bottom.
risks.failMessage: `$You erase three FAILs and pencil in PASS.\n\nMudge comes back up and holds the sheet to the light. "This is my handwriting," he says, "if I were a liar." The fine has a second page.
risks.successMessage: `$You erase three FAILs and pencil in PASS.\n\nMudge comes back up, glances at the sheet and nods. "Better than I remembered," he says. Your parlor gets a gold star for the window.

risks.startMessage: `$Ned and Rollo Mourne have parked the Mourne & Sons hearse across your driveway and gone into Yang's for lunch.\n\nThe keys are in the ignition. Your own hearse is boxed in, and a family is waiting at the cemetery.
risks.normalMessage: `$You wait. Forty minutes later the boys stroll out, apologize with their mouths full and move the hearse. The family at the cemetery has grown quite close in the meantime.
risks.failMessage: `$You hop in to move it.\n\nThe hearse is not empty. Rollo comes out of Yang's just in time to see you drive off with his client. The police are confused, and so is the widow.
risks.successMessage: `$You hop in and park it neatly. In front of a fire hydrant. Under a no-parking sign. Facing the wrong way.\n\nThe Mourne boys spend the afternoon at the impound lot. You make the cemetery with time to spare.

risks.startMessage: `$Dr. Grimble, the county coroner, needs a second signature on a death certificate, and you happen to be in his office.\n\nThe cause of death reads "unclear". If it read "natural causes", the family could skip the inquest and come straight to *PARLOR* this afternoon.
risks.normalMessage: `$You sign it as written. Dr. Grimble nods and offers you a peppermint from a jar labeled EVIDENCE. You decline the peppermint.
risks.failMessage: `$You cross out "unclear" and write "natural causes".\n\nThe inquest happens anyway. Your handwriting is Exhibit A. Dr. Grimble testifies that you "seemed very keen". The family takes the body to Mourne & Sons.
risks.successMessage: `$You cross out "unclear" and write "natural causes".\n\nDr. Grimble squints at it, shrugs and stamps it. The family is at your door by three, grateful and ready to spend.

police.peacefulSafe: Peaceful parlors are off the rota already.

gazette.smearChain: {name} is in your chain. Run it past them first.

hints.certWait: Paperwork needs a few days to pile up again
hints.boostOn: A clean bill of health is already posted
hints.stanceChosen: You have taken your stand today
hints.holdRecent: Your last stand still counts. Try again on day {day}
hints.noRivals: No rival parlors to complain about

coroner.title: County Coroner's Office
coroner.note: The Coroner's Office smells of formaldehyde and instant coffee. Both are strong.
coroner.greeting: `w{coroner}: `y"{player}. Sit. Not there, that one is occupied. Business is always brisk: people keep dying, and I keep being the first to know."

buttons.tip: Buy a Tip on Tomorrow's Deceased

coroner.tipBought: `${coroner} slides a folded note across the desk. "Next family through your door. I've read the file. You didn't get it from me." `5(-{price})`$
coroner.certBought: `${coroner} stamps a stack of certificates before the ink on the last one is dry. Families hear that you get paperwork done fast. `5(+{reviews} reputation)`$
coroner.favourIntro: `$Down the hall a cooler door is open. "Unclaimed," says {coroner}. "Nobody has asked after this one in nine days. The county pays for a pauper's plot, or the body could be made useful to someone with fewer questions." He waits.
coroner.burialDone: `$You pay for a plain pine box and a plot with a view of the dumpster. A handful of strangers turn up. It was the least you could do. `5(+{karma} karma, +{luck} luck)`$
coroner.quietDone: `${coroner} signs a form without reading it. "Wonderful. Nobody will ever ask." You are paid, in cash, promptly. `5(+{money}, {karma} karma)`$
coroner.quietTalk: `4Somebody noticed the paperwork. The whole town is now talking about the way you do business.`$

health.title: Health Department
health.note: The Health Department's waiting room has a poster about handwashing. It has been there since the poster was new.
health.greeting: `w{inspector}: `y"{player}. I look at {parlor}, I write what I see. Or I write what I am paid to see. It is a very flexible profession."

buttons.buy: Buy a Clean Bill of Health

health.passed: `${inspector} walks through your parlor in six minutes and signs. A framed certificate goes up by your door for `w{days}`$ days. `5(+{reviews} reputation)`$
health.failed: `4{inspector} finds a finger in the coffee maker. "That is not on the menu." A citation for `w{fine}`4 goes on file, and the neighbors hear about it. `5(-{reviews} reputation)`$
health.bought: `${inspector} counts the envelope without looking at it. "Spotless. Truly." The certificate hangs by your door for `w{days}`$ days. `5({karma} karma, +{reviews} reputation)`$
health.finePaid: `$You pay the citation in small bills. The clerk pins a receipt to it and, a few days later, the town forgets. `5(+{reviews} reputation)`$
health.complaintPrompt: Which parlor has been breaking the rules? It will cost `w{price}`$ to be heard.
health.complaintFiled: `${inspector} takes your complaint and files it where complaints are filed. "I will look into {name}'s kitchen." `5({karma} karma)`$
health.complaintDismissed: `${inspector} reads the complaint and puts it down. {name} holds a current certificate, so there is nothing to look into. The {price} stays in his drawer.
health.complaintBackfired: `4The complaint is traced straight back to you. Citation for `w{fine}`4 for wasting an inspector's time. `5(-{reviews} reputation)`$
health.complaintMail: `4A complaint was filed against {parlor} with the Health Department. Somebody in town does not like you. Your reputation dipped.`$
health.complaintNews:
`7COMPLAINT AT {parlor}
`^The Health Department has received a complaint about {name}'s parlor. Nobody will say who made it.
health.boostEnded: `$The health certificate by your door has gone yellow and fallen off. Your reputation slips back with it.

pawn.title: Cousin Sal's Pawn
pawn.note: Cousin Sal's Pawn: Cash for Anything, Especially Things With Names Engraved On Them.
pawn.greeting: `w{pawnbroker}: `y"{player}! Family. What have you got for me, and where did you get it? Actually, never mind the second part."
pawn.lootSold: `${pawnbroker} turns the pieces over under a lamp and counts out `w{money}`$. "No receipts, no names, no problem."
pawn.lotGood: `${pawnbroker} loads {count} "gently used" caskets into your trunk. They are, for once, exactly as described. `5(-{price})`$
pawn.lotBad: `4The bottom of the lot is water-damaged. Only {count} casket(s) in the lot are worth putting a body in. "No refunds," says {pawnbroker}. `5(-{price})`$
pawn.lotLine: `w{name}`$, `w{price}`$: {count} caskets at {percent}% of the Di-Mart price. {risk}% of lots turn out bad.

mournes.title: Mourne & Sons, Funeral Directors
mournes.note: Mourne & Sons, Deathville's other undertakers since 1931. The brass is polished. The prices are printed. They have been waiting for you.
mournes.greeting: `w{mourne}: `y"{player}. Do come in, and mind the carpet. My sons {sons} are out on a call, which means they will hear about this."
mournes.spyOk: `$You wander through their showroom with a clipboard and nobody stops you. Their price list is plain as day. Next time you meet a family, you will know what they will pay for. `5(-{price})`$
mournes.spyCaught: `4{sons} catch you copying prices out of the back of the brochure. "Gentlemen!" says {mourne}. "We have a visitor." You leave the way you came: loudly. `5(-{price}, {karma} karma, {reviews} reputation)`$
mournes.undercutWin: `$You put a banner over the door: FUNERALS, FOR LESS. {mournes} cannot match it without losing money, and by supper the whole town knows. `5(-{price}, +{reviews} reputation, +{luck} luck)`$
mournes.undercutLose: `4{mournes} match your price, then beat it, and their sons stand at the end of your road handing out coupons. `5(-{price}, {reviews} reputation)`$
mournes.holdDone: `$You keep your prices where they are. {mourne} nods across the street, one professional to another. "Admirable." `5(+{karma} karma)`$
mournes.truceDone: `$You and {mourne} shake on it in the middle of the street. For `w{days}`$ days neither of you will undercut the other. `5(+{karma} karma, -{price})`$
mournes.truceLead: `$As a gesture, {mournes} send you a family they are too busy to take. `5(+{leads} lead(s))`$

prep.text: `$While dressing the body you notice a ring is still on {dFirst} {surname}'s finger. It's a shame to bury such a beautiful stone.

options.label: Take It
options.text: `$You gently work it off and tuck {dHis} hand into a pocket so no one will notice. A pawn shop gives you a good price.

risk.failText: `$At the viewing, {surname}'s sister notices the pale band of skin where the ring was. She notices it loudly.

options.label: Leave It
options.text: `$You smile and gently pat it. Some things should go in the ground.

prep.text: `${dFirst} has a gold tooth. A big one. It catches the light every time you lean over the table.

options.label: Pliers
options.text: `$One good yank. Deathville Dental Recycling pays by the gram.

options.label: Leave It
options.text: `$You close {dHis} mouth. {dHeCap} smiles with it, in a way.

prep.text: `$There's a fat wallet in {dFirst}'s back pocket. The family never asked about it.

options.label: Pocket It
options.text: `$Finders keepers. {dFirst} won't be needing bus fare.

options.label: Return It
options.text: `$You hand it to the family. They tell everyone at the wake how honest you are.

prep.text: `$You're out of embalming fluid. There's a jug of Streak-B-Gone glass cleaner under the sink. It's blue. Embalming fluid is... sort of blue.

options.label: Use the Streak-B-Gone
options.text: `$Nobody notices a thing. {dFirst} has never looked so streak-free.

risk.failText: `$At the viewing {dFirst} faintly glows under the lights. A child points. Then everyone points.

options.label: Buy Proper Fluid
options.text: `$You run to Di-Mart for the real stuff. Elijah charges you the emergency price, the crook.

prep.text: `$A folded love letter is tucked in {dFirst}'s shirt pocket. It is not addressed to {dHis} spouse.

options.label: Read It at the Service
options.text: `$There isn't a dry eye in the house. Also there's a fistfight in the parking lot. People will talk about this one for years.

options.label: Sell It to the Tabloid
options.text: `$The Deathville Enquirer pays cash and runs it on page three.

options.label: Bury It With {dHim}
options.text: `$Some secrets belong six feet down.

prep.text: `${dFirst}'s old dog followed the hearse all the way here and is now lying by the back door, whining.

options.label: Adopt It
options.text: `$You name it Formaldehyde. It is a good dog. It eats like three dogs.

options.label: Shoo It Away
options.text: `$You throw a shoe. The dog takes the shoe. You are now down a shoe.

prep.text: `$The toe tag says {surname}, but this one has a tattoo that says "BIG STEVE". You have a feeling there has been a mix-up at the hospital.

options.label: Bury Him Anyway
options.text: `$Big Steve, {surname}, close enough. Nobody looks closely at a closed casket.

risk.failText: `$Halfway through the eulogy the real {dFirst} is wheeled in the side door. Awkward does not begin to cover it.

options.label: Call the Hospital
options.text: `$It takes all afternoon, but the right body arrives. The family never knows how close it was.

prep.text: `$A man in a lab coat at the back door offers $500 for "spare parts, no questions asked." He has a cooler.

options.label: Take the Cooler
options.text: `$You don't ask what he takes. He doesn't ask how you sleep. Everyone is happy except {dFirst}, who is past caring.

options.label: Slam the Door
options.text: `$You slam the door on his foot. It feels great.

prep.text: `${dFirst}'s finger twitches. Then the foot. With the right words from that book in your basement, {dHe} could mop floors for a week.

options.label: Say the Words
options.text: `${dFirst} sits up, groans, and mops the embalming room. Badly, but for free. The smell lingers for days.

options.label: Lay {dHim} to Rest
options.text: `$You put a hand on {dHis} chest until the twitching stops. Not today, {dFirst}.

prep.text: `$Father Smyth drops by and offers to bless {dFirst} for free, as long as you put the bake sale flyer in the program.

options.label: Accept the Blessing
options.text: `$Father Smyth blesses the body, the casket, you, the coffee machine and, for some reason, the hearse.

options.label: No Flyers
options.text: `$Father Smyth leaves, muttering something about lemon bars.

prep.text: `${dFirst}'s ashes come out about a pound light. The cat litter is right there on the shelf.

options.label: Top It Up
options.text: `$A cup of Kitty Klump and nobody is any the wiser. Clumps a little, though.

options.label: Tell the Family
options.text: `$You explain that some people are just light. They seem oddly proud.

prep.text: `$Rigor mortis has left {dFirst} with an enormous grin, like {dHe} just heard a filthy joke.

options.label: Leave the Grin
options.text: `$At the viewing everyone agrees {dFirst} looks happier than {dHe} ever did alive. One aunt faints. It's taken as a good omen.

options.label: Staple Gun
options.text: `$Two staples and a firm hand. {dFirst} looks dignified, and only slightly surprised.

risk.failText: `$During the viewing a staple gives out with an audible ping. The grin returns. So does the aunt, to faint again.

prep.text: `${dFirst}'s glass eye pops out and rolls under the embalming table. When you find it, it is looking right at you.

options.label: Put It Back
options.text: `$You pop it back in, a little crooked. All through the viewing {dFirst} appears to be winking at the widows.

options.label: Sell It to Cousin Sal
options.text: `$Sal pays fifty bucks and says he has "a patient" who needs it. You decide not to ask which way it will face.

options.label: Give It to Morty
options.text: `$Morty the skeleton finally has an eye. One. He seems more confident already.

prep.text: `$Someone has laid two silver dollars on {dFirst}'s eyes, the old way. You turn one over. 1921. Collector's coins.

options.label: Leave Them
options.text: `$Ferry fare for the far side. You'd hate for {dFirst} to have to swim.

options.label: Swap In Quarters
options.text: `$Inflation hits the afterlife hard. The coin shop on Main pays well and asks nothing.

risk.failText: `$The grandson leans in to say goodbye and loudly asks why Grandpa's eyes say "Delaware".

prep.text: `$The family's heirloom casket has a false bottom. Inside: rolls of twenties and a note that says NOT FOR THE GOVERNMENT.

options.label: Tell the Family
options.text: `$Three cousins dive into the casket at once. You've never seen people so happy at a funeral.

options.label: Take a Finder's Fee
options.text: `$You take one roll. A finder's fee. You did find it.

options.label: Take All of It
options.text: `$The government isn't getting it. Neither is the family. Neither is {dFirst}.

risk.failText: `$The family comes back for "Grandpa's special box" with a flashlight and a lawyer.

prep.text: `$Folded inside {dFirst}'s sock: a handwritten will, dated last Tuesday, leaving everything to the Deathville Zoo.

options.label: Give It to the Lawyer
options.text: `$The zoo gets a new gorilla house. The family gets nothing and blames you, loudly, at the wake.

options.label: Shred It
options.text: `$The family never knows. They tip you very well for no reason they can explain.

options.label: Mail It to the Zoo
options.text: `$A week later a zookeeper drops off a thank-you card and a penguin, which you are not allowed to keep.

prep.text: `${dFirst} left a cassette labelled PLAY AT MY FUNERAL. You play a bit of it in the back room. It is forty minutes of grudges, by name.

options.label: Play It All
options.text: `$The Mayor is mentioned eleven times. The cafe talks about nothing else for a month.

options.label: Play the Nice Parts
options.text: `$That takes nine seconds. You loop it twice. The family is very moved.

prep.text: `$In {dFirst}'s apron pocket: the recipe for {dHis} famous chili, which {dHe} refused to share for forty years.

options.label: Give It to the Family
options.text: `$They read it at the wake. The secret ingredient is ketchup. Some of them never recover.

options.label: Sell It to Bill's
options.text: `$Bill's Big Burger puts it on the menu as the Final Bowl. It sells out in a day.

options.label: Memorize It
options.text: `$You bury the card with {dHim}. Your chili wins the church cook-off every year from now on.

prep.text: `${dFirst}'s reading glasses are in {dHis} breast pocket. You try them on. Your exact prescription.

options.label: Keep Them
options.text: `$The world is suddenly sharp. You can read the fine print on your own contracts, which is a mistake.

options.label: Put Them On {dHim}
options.text: `${dFirst} looks ready to read the small print on the afterlife.

prep.text: `${dFirst}'s cardigan pockets are full of butterscotch candies. Hundreds. It's like {dHe} was preparing for a siege.

options.label: Leave Them
options.text: `$Someday an archaeologist is going to have a very confusing afternoon.

options.label: Fill the Lobby Bowl
options.text: `$Every mourner takes one and quietly weeps. It's the most effective marketing you have ever done.

options.label: Eat Them
options.text: `$You eat eleven before you remember where they came from. You eat a twelfth anyway.

prep.text: `$In {dFirst}'s coat pocket: a film canister of ashes labelled BISCUIT. The dog, you hope.

options.label: Bury Biscuit With {dHim}
options.text: `$Together again. You add a dog biscuit for the road.

options.label: Return Biscuit
options.text: `$The family had been looking everywhere for Biscuit. They thought {dFirst} had sold him.

prep.text: `${dFirst}'s fingerprints come back under three different names. Two men in sunglasses have been parked outside since dawn.

options.label: Ask No Questions
options.text: `$The men in sunglasses tip you in cash and assure you {dFirst} was never here. Neither were they.

options.label: Call Deathville PD
options.text: `$The police thank you. The sunglasses men do not. Someone keys your hearse that night.

prep.text: `$Something in {dFirst}'s jacket keeps buzzing. It's {dHis} phone: 41 missed calls from a number saved as DO NOT ANSWER.

options.label: Answer It
options.text: `$It's about {dHis} car's extended warranty. You say {dFirst} has passed. They ask for {dHis} new address.

options.label: Leave It Buzzing
options.text: `$It buzzes faintly all through the eulogy. Everyone agrees it's {dFirst} still trying to get a word in.

prep.text: `${dFirst} asked to be buried with {dHis} bowling trophy. It's solid brass, two feet tall, and frankly gorgeous.

options.label: Bury It
options.text: `${dFirst} rests with {dHis} greatest triumph: 1983 Deathville Lanes, Second Place.

options.label: Put It on Your Shelf
options.text: `$It looks fantastic in the lobby. Customers assume you bowl. You let them.

prep.text: `$The bank Teller calls. {dFirst}'s safe deposit key is in {dHis} pocket and the bank "would appreciate its prompt and proper return".

options.label: Return the Key
options.text: `$The Teller thanks you in a tone that suggests she expected otherwise.

options.label: Open the Box First
options.text: `$Inside: savings bonds, a bad poem, and cash. You keep the cash. The poem you return.

risk.failText: `$The box holds one note: I KNEW YOU WOULD LOOK. The Teller reads it over your shoulder and tells the whole bank.

prep.text: `$The family paid for a gold casket. A silver one is sitting right there, and Di-Mart takes returns within thirty days.

options.label: Switch Caskets
options.text: `$Elijah processes the refund without blinking. Elijah never blinks.

risk.failText: `$At the viewing a nephew raps on the lid and asks why gold sounds so hollow. Uncle Ray pulls out the receipt.

options.label: Use the Gold
options.text: `${dFirst} goes into the ground in the casket {dHe} paid for. Your accountant weeps quietly.

prep.text: `${dFirst} is about four inches longer than the casket.

options.label: Bend the Knees
options.text: `$Nobody looks at the knees. You hope nobody looks at the knees.

risk.failText: `$Halfway through the viewing a knee straightens with a crack and the lid rises two inches.

options.label: Rush a Longer One
options.text: `$Elijah's boy, who is 64, delivers it on foot. It costs you, but {dFirst} lies flat.

prep.text: `$It rained all night. {dFirst}'s grave is half full of water, and there's a frog in it.

options.label: Bail It Out
options.text: `$Two hours with a Bill's Big Burger cup. The frog stays. You decide the frog is a mourner.

options.label: Lower {dHim} In Anyway
options.text: `$There is a small splash. Then a large one, when Uncle Ray slips in after {dHim}.

prep.text: `$There is a humming coming from inside the casket lining. It is getting louder, and the viewing starts in ten minutes.

options.label: Open It Anyway
options.text: `$A single bee drifts out, circles {dFirst} like a halo and flies away. People call it a sign.

risk.failText: `$They are not bees. They are wasps. Father Smyth sets a new parish record for the hundred-yard dash.

options.label: Call the Exterminator
options.text: `$He charges an extra fee for working near the deceased, and another for working near you.

prep.text: `$You forgot to order the casket spray. The grave next door got a fresh delivery this morning.

options.label: Borrow Them
options.text: `$They're barely used. The dead don't look at their flowers anyway.

risk.failText: `$The widow from next door visits during the service and recognizes her own carnations.

options.label: Buy Fresh Ones
options.text: `$The florist charges you the panic price. You pay the panic price.

prep.text: `${dFirst} served in the army. The flag the family brought has a hole in it the exact shape of a cigarette burn.

options.label: Buy a New Flag
options.text: `$Di-Mart has exactly one left. Elijah charges you as if it's the last one in the country.

options.label: Fold It Hole-Side In
options.text: `$Nobody will ever know.

risk.failText: `$The honor guard unfolds it, snaps it open, and everybody gets a long look through the hole.

prep.text: `$The hearse gets a flat on the way to the cemetery. The spare is under {dFirst}.

options.label: Change It in the Rain
options.text: `$Twenty minutes in your good suit. The mourners hold umbrellas. It's weirdly bonding.

options.label: Ask the Mourners to Push
options.text: `$Six pallbearers, one hearse, half a mile. They're dressed for it, technically.

prep.text: `${dFirst} came in wearing a toupee. It has come off. It is on the floor. It may be a raccoon.

options.label: Glue It Back On
options.text: `$Back on and nearly straight. {dFirst} looks like {dHe} did in every photo.

risk.failText: `$Under the viewing lamps the glue lets go, and the toupee slides gently onto the casket pillow like a sleeping pet.

options.label: Bury {dHim} Bald
options.text: `${dFirst} meets eternity as {dHe} truly was. The family is shocked. Then they're kind of moved.

options.label: Sell It to Elijah
options.text: `$Elijah buys it without a word and is wearing it by the afternoon.

prep.text: `${dFirst} has a large tattoo of an ex's name on {dHis} forearm. The new spouse will be at the viewing.

options.label: Cover It With Makeup
options.text: `$Three coats of Deathly Beige. You can't see a thing.

risk.failText: `$Under the hot lights the makeup sweats off one letter at a time. By the closing hymn, everyone can read it.

options.label: Long Sleeves
options.text: `$You buy a shirt at Di-Mart. Elijah upsells you cufflinks. Somehow you also own a tie clip now.

options.label: Leave It Showing
options.text: `$It's the most honest thing at the funeral.

prep.text: `${dFirst}'s dentures don't fit any more. Rigor mortis has opinions about dentures.

options.label: Leave Them Out
options.text: `${dFirst} looks like a very sad jack-o'-lantern. You put a hymnal under {dHis} chin and hope.

options.label: Borrow Morty's Teeth
options.text: `$They fit perfectly. Morty doesn't complain. Morty never complains.

risk.failText: `$A mourner leans close and counts. There are noticeably too many teeth.

prep.text: `$The family brought a photo for the makeup. It's {dFirst}'s yearbook photo from 1971.

options.label: Do the 1971 Look
options.text: `$Feathered hair, blue eyeshadow, sideburns that may not be historically accurate. The family is thrilled. Everyone else is unsettled.

options.label: Do {dHim} Natural
options.text: `$A little powder, a little blush. {dFirst} looks like {dHe} did last week, minus the {surname} family scowl.

prep.text: `$The family dropped off {dFirst}'s best outfit. It's covered in dog hair and the pockets are full of bingo daubers.

options.label: Lend {dHim} Your Suit
options.text: `$Your good black suit. It fits {dHim} better than it fits you, which hurts.

options.label: Daubers and All
options.text: `$Father Smyth spots the daubers and announces {dFirst} was a regular. The whole bingo hall turns out.

prep.text: `$The family wants one last photo of {dFirst} sitting up in the casket, holding {dHis} favorite fishing rod.

options.label: Pose {dHim}
options.text: `$It's a lovely photo. The rod bends like {dHe} just hooked a big one.

risk.failText: `$The rod tips. Then {dFirst} tips. Then Aunt Pearl tips, onto the buffet.

options.label: Politely Refuse
options.text: `$You explain the casket has a weight limit. It doesn't. They don't know that.

prep.text: `$A fly lands on {dFirst}'s nose just as the family walks in.

options.label: Swat It
options.text: `$One clean swat. The family thinks you were wiping away a tear.

risk.failText: `$You miss the fly. You do not miss {dFirst}.

options.label: Pretend Not to See
options.text: `$The fly stays for the whole viewing. Some people find it very spiritual.

prep.text: `$As you lift {dFirst} into the casket, {dHe} lets out a long, mournful last breath. From the wrong end. In front of the family.

options.label: Blame the Organist
options.text: `$The organist is fired on the spot. He didn't do it. He never does it. Nobody believes him.

options.label: Say Bless You
options.text: `$There's a long silence. Then the widow laughs for the first time in a week.

prep.text: `$Morty the skeleton fell over in the night. Most of his left hand is now in the casket with {dFirst}.

options.label: Sort It Out
options.text: `$It takes all afternoon and a diagram from Spirit University, but every finger goes home.

options.label: Close Enough
options.text: `$Thirty-one bones, give or take. The lid is closed. Morty will adapt.

risk.failText: `$At the viewing, {dFirst}'s folded hands are noticeably bonier than the rest of {dHim}.

prep.text: `${dFirst} still has a pacemaker in. Pacemakers do not like incinerators. Taking it out properly is an hour's work.

options.label: Take It Out
options.text: `$An hour, a pair of tongs and a very steady hand. Procedure followed.

options.label: Fire It Up Anyway
options.text: `$You save an hour. There's a muffled pop. Nothing to worry about.

risk.failText: `$The furnace door blows open with a bang that rattles windows on three streets. Across the road, Father Smyth hits the floor.

options.label: Sell It to Cousin Sal
options.text: `$Sal swears it's for a patient. You saw his patients. You take the money.

prep.text: `$Two urns, two families, one shelf. The labels have fallen off, and both families are coming at four.

options.label: Weigh Them and Guess
options.text: `$You guess. You are probably right. Probably is doing a lot of work in that sentence.

risk.failText: `$One family finds a hip replacement in the urn. Their grandmother never had a hip replacement.

options.label: Tell Both Families
options.text: `$They agree to split both urns down the middle. It's very fair. Nobody is happy.

prep.text: `$The incinerator is still roaring from {dFirst}, you skipped lunch, and there's a frozen pizza in the break room.

options.label: Use the Heat
options.text: `$Best crust you've ever had. You don't think about it. You think about it.

risk.failText: `$Father Smyth drops by mid-slice and asks what smells so good.

options.label: Wait for the Microwave
options.text: `$Soggy, lukewarm, respectful.

prep.text: `$The incinerator's smoke sets off the fire alarm at the Pale Horse Cafe next door. Again. The owner is at your door with a mop.

options.label: Apologize With Pie
options.text: `$A peace offering from Di-Mart's bakery aisle. The owner accepts and steals your mop.

options.label: Unplug Their Alarm
options.text: `$No more complaints. Peace and quiet for everyone.

risk.failText: `$That night the Pale Horse actually catches fire. The Twins are seen across the street, smiling in unison.

prep.text: `${dFirst}'s sister asks to sit alone with {dHim} for an hour before the viewing. You usually charge for the room.

options.label: Charge Her
options.text: `$Hourly rate, two-hour minimum. Grief is a premium service.

options.label: Let Her Sit
options.text: `$She talks to {dFirst} about things you pretend not to hear. She leaves lighter.

options.label: Bring Her Coffee Too
options.text: `$And a muffin. She tells everyone at church, which is how you get three funerals next month.

prep.text: `$June from Yang's turns up with a takeout order {dFirst} placed the morning {dHe} died. It's already paid for.

options.label: Eat It
options.text: `$General Tso's, still warm. June watches you eat it and says nothing, which is worse.

options.label: Put It in the Casket
options.text: `$Fried rice for the afterlife. Mr. Yang hears about it and tells every customer for a week.

options.label: Give It to the Family
options.text: `$They eat it at the wake, crying into the lo mein. It's the best part of the day.

prep.text: `$The Mayor wants a photo next to {dFirst}'s casket for his re-election flyer: TOUGH ON DEATH.

options.label: Allow It
options.text: `$He shakes your hand and leaves an envelope on the casket. Campaign contribution, in reverse.

options.label: Charge Double
options.text: `$Two envelopes. The Mayor understands business.

risk.failText: `$The flyer comes out with the family in the background, mid-sob. They see it on every lamp post.

options.label: Refuse
options.text: `$The Mayor calls you unpatriotic and gets your parking spaces repainted as loading zones.

prep.text: `$Old Man Withers wanders into the back room "to get a feel for the place" and lies down on your spare table.

options.label: Let Him Nap
options.text: `$He snores like a leaf blower for two hours, then thanks you and tells the whole bingo hall you're good people.

options.label: Measure Him
options.text: `$You'll need it eventually. He's been saying so since 1974. He is shorter than he claims.

prep.text: `$Elijah calls: a crate of embalming fluid "fell off a truck". Half price, cash only, back alley, tonight.

options.label: Buy the Crate
options.text: `$You save a bundle. The fluid looks right. It's even the right blue.

risk.failText: `$The crate is mostly maple syrup. {dFirst} smells like pancakes all through the viewing.

options.label: Hang Up
options.text: `$Elijah breathes down the line for a while. He doesn't say goodbye. He never says goodbye.

prep.text: `$Father Smyth asks to borrow your hearse to deliver the church bake sale. It will smell of lemon bars forever.

options.label: Lend It
options.text: `$The bake sale breaks records. The hearse smells amazing. Mourners keep asking if there's dessert.

options.label: It's Busy
options.text: `$Father Smyth delivers forty dozen lemon bars on a bicycle and blesses you through gritted teeth.

prep.text: `${dFirst}'s grandkids drew a picture for the casket: {dFirst} as a very happy stick figure with a halo, a fishing rod and seven fingers.

options.label: Pin It Inside the Lid
options.text: `${dFirst} goes into the ground with seven fingers and a halo. Not a bad way to go.

options.label: Bill for the Pinning
options.text: `$Pinning fee: fifty dollars. Crayon handling surcharge: included. You are a monster, but an itemized one.

prep.text: `$The family asks you to write the eulogy. All you know about {dFirst} is the name and the weight.

options.label: Make It Up
options.text: `$War hero, champion yodeler, friend to every orphan in the county. People are in tears.

risk.failText: `$You call {dHim} a war hero. The whole {surname} family are famous for refusing to fight in anything.

options.label: Keep It Short
options.text: `$"{dFirst} was here. Now {dHe} isn't. Snacks are in the lobby." Nobody has ever loved a eulogy more.

prep.text: `$The potato salad for {dFirst}'s wake has been sitting in the sun since noon. It has started to sweat.

options.label: Serve It
options.text: `$Nobody gets sick. Nobody gets sick yet.

risk.failText: `$Half the mourners are back by Thursday. On the bright side, some of them are back as customers.

options.label: Throw It Out
options.text: `$You buy fresh from the Pale Horse Cafe. It's worse, but it won't kill anyone.

prep.text: `$Spirit University's anatomy lab will pay well for an intact brain, and {dFirst}'s family chose a closed casket.

options.label: Sell the Brain
options.text: `$The professor pays cash and says {dFirst} will be very useful to science, eventually, in a jar.

options.label: Bury {dHim} Whole
options.text: `${dFirst} goes down with everything {dHe} came in with, including the brain {dHe} rarely used.

prep.text: `${dFirst}'s will asks for {dHis} skeleton to go to Spirit University. Morty, in the corner, looks lonely.

options.label: Donate It
options.text: `$The university sends a lovely certificate. Morty sulks for a week.

options.label: Give Morty a Friend
options.text: `$Morty and the new guy sit together by the window. You are not sure which one moved the chair.

prep.text: `$The Twins knock on the back door at the same time. "We'll take that empty casket crate off your hands," they say together. "For kindling."

options.label: Sell Them the Crate
options.text: `$They pay in matches. Then in cash. You don't ask what they're kindling.

options.label: Recycle It
options.text: `$The Twins watch you put it in the dumpster without blinking. Both of them. In sync.

prep.text: `${dFirst} is still registered to vote, and the Mayor's election is tomorrow.

options.label: Cast {dHis} Ballot
options.text: `$The Mayor wins by one vote. A fruit basket arrives with a card that just says ;)

options.label: Let {dHim} Rest
options.text: `${dFirst} abstains, as {dHe} did in life.

prep.text: `$The hospital bracelet says {dFirst} was admitted for a sprained ankle.

options.label: Call the Nurse
options.text: `$The Nurse laughs for a long time, then says "oh, honey, don't look at the chart" and hangs up.

options.label: Keep Quiet
options.text: `$A fruit basket arrives from the hospital: "Thanks for your discretion." There's an envelope under the pears.

prep.text: `$The Deathville Enquirer ran {dFirst}'s obituary under the headline LOCAL LEGEND FINALLY QUIET.

options.label: Demand a Correction
options.text: `$They print one the next day: LOCAL LEGEND FINALLY QUIET, SAYS FAMILY.

options.label: Frame It for the Lobby
options.text: `$Customers love it. The {surname} family does not.

prep.text: `$The church choir asks to rehearse in your viewing room tonight, with {dFirst} still lying in state.

options.label: Let Them Sing
options.text: `$They sing until midnight. By morning {dFirst} looks more peaceful than any embalming could manage.

options.label: Charge Them Rent
options.text: `$Twenty dollars a soprano. The basses get a group rate.

prep.text: `$A teenager at {dFirst}'s viewing asks if it's okay to take a selfie with the casket.

options.label: Say No, Kindly
options.text: `$You explain that some moments are private. The teenager rolls their eyes but puts the phone away.

options.label: Charge Five Bucks
options.text: `$You put up a little sign: PHOTOS WITH {dFirst} $5. Business is brisk.

risk.failText: `$The photo goes around the whole school with your price sign in it. The {surname} family sees it by dinner.

options.label: Hold the Phone for Them
options.text: `$You even find the good light. The teenager says it's the nicest thing an adult has done all year.
