specials.label: Mob Boss
specials.intro:
`$Two large men in sunglasses check your closets before an old man in a camel coat sits down.

{customer}"My associate {dFirst} had an accident. With {aFridge}. Several times. I want a funeral people will remember, and a casket that does not open from the inside."

lines.happy: {customer}"You did right by {dFirst}. Nobody will bother you tonight. Nobody."
lines.threat: {customer}"You disappoint me." The large men walk you out to the alley and explain your disappointment to your ribs.

specials.label: Celebrity
specials.intro:
`$Flashbulbs go off outside your window. Crystal Vance, star of the reality show "Tanning Moms", sweeps in behind giant sunglasses.

{customer}"My {dRelation} {dFirst} is dead and the cameras are rolling. Make it TRAGIC. Make it TRENDING."

lines.happy: {customer}"Oh my god, the crying shots are going to be AMAZING."
lines.walkout: `$Crystal storms out to her limo. By dinner the whole town has seen the clip of her calling your parlor "a Di-Mart for corpses".

specials.label: Pet Funeral
specials.intro:
`${customerName} sets a shoebox on your desk. Something inside it is not moving.

{customer}"This is {dFirst}. {dFirst} was a good {pet}. The best {pet}. The vet said you do pets?"

lines.happy: {customer}"{dFirst} would have loved this. {dFirst} loved everything. Except the mailman."

specials.label: Pre-Need Planner
specials.intro:
`${customerName} sits down with a clipboard and a highlighter.

{customer}"Nobody's dead yet. Me, eventually. I want to pick out my own {casket} casket now, before my kids pick something tacky."

future.text: `${name} finally used the funeral {he} planned with you. The family pays the balance.

specials.label: The Widow Black
specials.intro:
`$Vivian Black glides in, all in black, as usual.

{customer}"Husband number five, darling. Same as last time, but bigger. You know I like things bigger."

lines.happy: {customer}"Lovely. Keep my file handy, darling. Number six has a weak heart."

specials.label: County Contract
specials.intro:
`$A clerk from the county drops off a toe-tagged John Doe and a form in triplicate.

`wClerk: `$"Unclaimed, no family. County pays the flat rate: a pine box and a hole. Take it or leave it, I've got six more in the van."

accept.label: Take the Body
accept.text: `$You bury John Doe with as much dignity as the county rate allows, which is not much. Father Smyth says a few words. Some of them are "who?"

decline.label: Turn It Down
decline.text: `$The clerk shrugs and wheels John Doe across the street to a rival. You hear the word "cheapskate" through the window.

specials.label: Cousin Sal
specials.intro:
`$Cousin Sal, M.D. (University of P.O. Box 411), backs a station wagon up to your door.

`wCousin Sal: `$"Got a body for you. Paperwork's, uh, still being printed. Cash only, no questions, no autopsy, especially no autopsy."

accept.label: Take the Cash
accept.text: `$You bury the mystery guest under a fake name. Sal pays in damp twenties. You sleep fine. Mostly.

decline.label: Call the Police
decline.text: `$Sal is gone before the squad car arrives. The officer thanks you and tells the whole precinct you're one of the good ones.

specials.label: Old Man Withers
specials.intro:
`$Old Man Withers, who has been "about to die any day now" since 1974, shuffles in to price-check his funeral again.

{customer}"Just looking. Show me your cheapest {casket}. I'll know if you're lying, I invented lying."

lines.happy: {customer}"Not bad, sonny. I'll tell everyone at bingo. Don't get excited, I'm not dying this week."

specials.label: Father Smyth
specials.intro:
`$Father Smyth hurries in, wiping lemon-bar crumbs off his collar.

{customer}"Old {dFirst}, one of my flock, has gone to glory. The family left it to the parish, and the parish is broke. A {casket} casket, please, and try not to make me sin in your office."

lines.happy: {customer}"Bless you. I'll mention you from the pulpit on Sunday. Between the bingo results and the bake sale, but I'll mention you."
lines.walkout: `$Father Smyth leaves shaking his head. On Sunday the sermon is about the money changers in the temple. Everyone looks at your pew.

specials.label: The Mayor
specials.intro:
`$A news van parks outside. The Mayor strides in, shaking hands with your coat rack on the way.

{customer}"Terrible loss. My former deputy, {dFirst}, was {dSmashed} {aFridge}. The cameras will be there, so I need a {casket} casket that says 'I cared' and photographs from my good side."

lines.happy: {customer}"Wonderful. I'll say a few words at the service. Mostly about my re-election, but a few about {dFirst}."
lines.walkout: `$That evening the Mayor holds a press conference on the steps of City Hall about "unscrupulous death merchants". He does not say your name. He points at your parlor on the map.

specials.label: The Twins
specials.intro:
`$Two identical men in identical smoky jackets carry in something wrapped in a scorched carpet.

`wThe Twins: `y"We found this in a barn. The barn was on fire. We didn't start that fire. We started a different fire. Bury it quiet and we'll pay cash."

accept.label: Bury It Quiet
accept.text: `$You bury the carpet and its contents behind the parlor before lunch. The Twins pay in slightly singed bills and wink in perfect unison.

decline.label: Show Them Out
decline.text: `$The Twins look at each other, then at your curtains. "Nice curtains," they say together. "Very dry." They leave. You buy a fire extinguisher.

specials.label: Elijah from Di-Mart
specials.intro:
`$Elijah from Di-Mart sits down without being asked. He does not blink. He has never blinked.

{customer}"My {dRelation}. {dFirst}. Passed some time ago. I only noticed this morning. {dHeCap} was very quiet, even before. A {casket} casket. I'll want the employee discount."

lines.happy: {customer}"Acceptable. Come by the store. I'll show you the back room. Not that back room. The other one."
lines.walkout: `$Elijah stands, straightens his tie and leaves without a word. For a week, every casket you buy at Di-Mart has a faint fingerprint smudge on the lid, exactly where your hand goes.

specials.label: The Nurse
specials.intro:
`$The Nurse from the city hospital pops in, still in scrubs, smiling as always.

{customer}"Hi, prince! Quick one. The night shift wants a Christmas party and the hospital won't pay. Chip in, and I'll make sure our discharged-permanently patients get your card first."

accept.label: Sponsor the Party
accept.text: `$You hand over an envelope. Within the hour three orderlies have your business card taped inside the morgue drawers. The Nurse blows you a kiss from the door.

decline.label: Too Expensive
decline.text: `$"No problem, prince!" She is still smiling. By evening the morgue drawers have a different parlor's card in them.

specials.label: The Bank Teller
specials.intro:
`$The teller from the bank sits down, adjusts her glasses and lays a deposit slip on your desk like an accusation.

{customer}"My {dRelation}, {dFirst}, has closed {dHis} account, so to speak. A {casket} casket. I will be checking your arithmetic. I check everyone's arithmetic."

lines.happy: {customer}"Your figures are correct. I'm almost disappointed. Here, a gold tag. Don't spend it all on something silly."
lines.walkout: {customer}"I've seen your balance, you know. I'll be thinking about it every time you come to my window."

specials.label: The Clown Family
specials.intro:
`$A tiny car parks outside and nine mourners in full face paint climb out of it.

{customer}"Our {dRelation}, {dFirst}, was the best clown in three counties. {dHeCap} died doing the thing with the {dFridge}. We want a {casket} casket, and we want it to honk."

lines.happy: {customer}"It's perfect. {dFirst} would have laughed. Then fallen down. Then laughed again." A horn honks somewhere in the room.
lines.walkout: `$The clowns leave single file, all nine back into the tiny car. It takes twenty minutes. Nobody laughs.

specials.label: The Fake Death
specials.intro:
`${customerName} closes the blinds before {cHe} sits down and speaks very quietly.

{customer}"Nobody's dead. That's the problem. I need a funeral for me, with an empty casket, a death certificate and a lot of crying, by Friday. The insurance company pays, we split it. You in?"

accept.label: Fake the Funeral
accept.text: `$You bury a casket full of sandbags with full honors. Cousin Sal signs the death certificate without reading it. Your share arrives in a gym bag.

decline.label: No Thanks
decline.text: `${customerName} sighs. "Fine. I'll ask Blaine." A week later the Blaine paper reports a miraculous resurrection, and an arrest.

specials.label: The Count
specials.intro:
`$It is the middle of the day, but your office somehow gets darker. A tall old man in a cape steps out of the corner you were sure was empty.

{customer}"I require a casket. For myself. For sleeping. A {casket} one, lined in something dark. I am a light sleeper. Very light. Nearly dead, you might say."

lines.happy: {customer}"Excellent. I shall recommend you to my friends. They are very old friends. Some of them are still in the ground."
lines.walkout: `$The Count turns into something small and leathery and flaps out through your mail slot. You lie awake all night listening to the gutters.

specials.label: Rival From Blaine
specials.intro:
`${customerName} walks in wearing a lapel pin from a Blaine funeral home and looks around like {cHe}'s pricing the furniture.

{customer}"My {dRelation} {dFirst} died here, in Deathville, which is typical. I could do it myself back in Blaine, but our caskets cost more. A {casket} one. Don't try anything, I know every trick in the book. I wrote two of them."

lines.happy: {customer}"Hm. Not bad for a Deathville outfit. Don't tell anyone in Blaine I said so."
lines.walkout: {customer}"Amateurs. I'll tell everyone in Blaine. They already think you people bury folks in shopping carts."

specials.label: The Jackpot Heirs
specials.intro:
`${customerName} and four relatives are all talking at once. Two are holding the same lottery ticket.

{customer}"{dFirst} won the state lottery Tuesday and got {dSmashed} {aFridge} Wednesday. We want a {casket} casket, the best of everything, and somebody to stand between my cousins at the service."

lines.happy: {customer}"Great, done, we'll split the bill. Five ways. Don't argue, there are lawyers outside." Someone tips you a hundred on the way out.
lines.walkout: `$The heirs leave in five separate cars. That night two of them are on the TV news fighting over the ticket in a parking lot.

specials.label: The Zookeeper
specials.intro:
`$The keeper from the Deathville Zoo backs a flatbed truck up to your door. There is a very large tarp on it.

{customer}"This is {dFirst}. {dFirst} was a {pet}. The kids loved {dFirst}. The zoo budget doesn't. Have you got a {casket} casket in, uh, extra large?"

lines.happy: {customer}"The kids are going to love the headstone. We're putting it next to the snack bar."
lines.walkout: `$The keeper drives off with {dFirst}. Rumor has it the {pet} ends up in the quarry. The whole town can smell the rumor for a week.

specials.label: Ghost Hunters
specials.intro:
`$Three people in matching black T-shirts set up a camera on your desk without asking.

{customer}"We're Ghost Patrol Deathville. Cable access, Thursdays at two a.m. We want to spend the night in your parlor and film the dead. We'll pay. Is your skeleton available for an interview?"

accept.label: Let Them Film
accept.text: `$They film all night. The episode shows four minutes of Morty in different lighting and one very clear shot of you eating cold noodles in the embalming room at 3 a.m.

decline.label: Respect the Dead
decline.text: `$You show them out. On the way to their van one of them swears Morty waved. Morty did not wave. Probably.

specials.label: The Coroner
specials.intro:
`$Dr. Ignatius Grimble, the county coroner, comes in smelling of formaldehyde and peppermint, which is how you know he has been working.

`wDr. Grimble: `$"Four unclaimed this week, and my freezer is full of picnic leftovers. Take them at the county rate and you go to the top of my morning list. Say no and you go to the bottom. In pencil."

accept.label: Take All Four
accept.text: `$You fit four strangers into two days of work. Dr. Grimble signs the forms without looking up and writes your parlor at the top of his list, in ink.

decline.label: Not Today
decline.text: `$Dr. Grimble shrugs and writes something down. It is your name, at the bottom, in pencil. He has a very sharp pencil.

specials.label: Augustus Mourne
specials.intro:
`$Augustus Mourne of Mourne & Sons, Deathville's other undertakers since 1931, sits down and opens a notebook to a page with your name at the top.

{customer}"My {dRelation} {dFirst} has died, and my own family won't touch the body. Professional courtesy, they call it. A grudge, I call it. A {casket} casket. I'll be taking notes."

lines.happy: {customer}"Annoyingly competent. I'll tell the boys to raise our prices. From a Mourne, that's a compliment."
lines.walkout: `$Augustus Mourne closes his notebook with a snap. By Friday every family in town has a Mourne & Sons flyer promising "none of that nonsense from across the street".

specials.label: Inspector Mudge
specials.intro:
`$Inspector Mudge from City Hall stands in your doorway with a clipboard, a flashlight and the face of a man who has already found something.

`wInspector Mudge: `$"Surprise inspection. I could spend all afternoon in your basement, or I could accept a modest gift to the Inspectors' Widows Fund. I am, technically, its only member."

accept.label: Make a Gift
accept.text: `$You hand over an envelope. Inspector Mudge glances at the basement door, writes SPOTLESS on his clipboard and leaves whistling.

decline.label: Open the Basement
decline.text: `$Mudge spends three hours in your basement. He finds the old embalming fluid, the raccoon and Morty's other leg. The fine stings, but the paper calls you "honest, if damp".

specials.label: Lucius Vane
specials.intro:
`$The lights flicker. Lucius Vane, who owns the Reaper Club and possibly the night, is sitting across from you. You did not see him sit down.

{customer}"A business associate of mine, {dFirst}, had an accident with {aFridge}. A {casket} casket and a closed lid. A very closed lid. Money is not the issue. Questions are."

lines.happy: {customer}"Discreet. I like discreet. If you ever find yourself at my club, the house will remember you. Fondly. Mostly."
lines.walkout: `$Lucius Vane rises without a sound. For a week, every card you are dealt in this town is the two of clubs. Every single one.

specials.label: June from Yang's
specials.intro:
`$June from Yang's comes in still wearing her apron. She looks at the floor, then at you, then at the floor again.

{customer}"It's {dFirst}. Our {pet}. {dFirst} lived behind the counter for eleven years. Dad says it's silly. Dad also cried in the walk-in freezer. A {casket} casket, please. A small one."

lines.happy: {customer}"That was... really nice. Thank you." For once, neither of you pretends it didn't happen.
lines.walkout: `$June leaves without a word. The next time you eat at Yang's, your fortune cookie is empty.

loved: {customerName} keeps touching a photo of {dFirst} like it might still be warm.
{customer}"{dHeCap} made the worst coffee in the world. I'd give anything for one more cup."
{customerName}'s mascara has given up entirely.
{customer}"I keep setting two plates at dinner."
{customerName} is wearing {dFirst}'s old cardigan. It's three sizes too big.
{customer}"I still have {dHis} voicemail saved. I play it in the car. It's just {dHim} asking where the remote is."
{customerName} has to stop twice while saying {dFirst}'s name.
{customer}"Everybody keeps saying it gets easier. When? Give me a date."
{customerName} is holding {dFirst}'s house keys and won't put them down.
{customer}"{dHeCap} always knew what to say. I've been standing in the kitchen for two days waiting for {dHim} to say it."
{customerName} apologises to the chair after bumping into it, then starts crying again.
{customer}"I went to call {dHim} about it. To tell {dHim} {dHe} died. I had the phone in my hand."
{customerName} carefully straightens {dFirst}'s photo on your desk. It was already straight.
{customer}"Can {dHe} have {dHis} reading glasses? {dHeCap} hated not being able to see."
{customerName} hasn't slept. It's written all over {cHis} face, along with a lot of smeared eyeliner.
{customer}"I found {dHis} grocery list. Milk, eggs, call {cFirst}. I'm {cFirst}."
{customerName} smiles at something only {cHe} remembers, then stops smiling.
{customerName} has brought {dFirst}'s favorite mug and holds it in {cHis} lap the whole time.
{customer}"{dHeCap} used to hum when {dHe} cooked. The kitchen is so quiet now I can hear the clock."
{customerName} stops mid-sentence to blow {cHis} nose, then apologizes to the tissue box.
{customer}"We were going to Lake Bleak this summer. I already bought the bait. I can't throw out the bait."
{customerName} keeps saying "we", then correcting it to "I", and it hurts every time.
{customer}"I don't want {dHim} to be cold. Is it cold down there? Don't answer. Just make it warm."
{customerName} has {dFirst}'s name written on the back of {cHis} hand, as if {cHe} might forget it.
{customer}"I left {dHis} porch light on last night. I know. I know. I just did."
notLoved: {customerName} checks {cHis} phone. Twice. While you're talking.
{customer}"How long does this usually take? The will is being read at four."
{customerName} hasn't once said {dFirst}'s name.
{customer}"Can we skip the part where I pretend to be sad?"
{customerName} asks if you validate parking before asking anything about the funeral.
{customer}"{dFirst}? Yeah. That was the name. Is there a form?"
{customerName} yawns, then covers it with a fake sob that fools nobody.
{customer}"Honestly I'm only here because the rest of the family voted and I lost."
{customerName} calls {dFirst} "the deceased" every single time, like a cop on TV.
{customer}"I brought a black tie. It's a clip-on. That's about my level of grief."
{customerName} is humming. Quietly, but definitely humming.
{customer}"Do I have to come to the viewing, or can I just send flowers? Cheap flowers?"
{customerName} has already measured {dFirst}'s living room for a pool table.
{customer}"We weren't close. We weren't anything. We were people who shared a Thanksgiving once."
{customerName} glances at the clock on your wall, then at {cHis} watch, to check the clock.
{customer}"Is it bad that I'm a little relieved? Don't answer that. It's not bad."
{customerName} asks if {dFirst} can be buried "somewhere out of the way". Like a basement.
{customer}"{dHeCap} owed me forty dollars. Can that come off the bill?"

softPitch:
`w{player}: `$"Most families in your situation go with {article} {item}. ${price}, and it says 'we cared' without saying 'we cared a lot'."

`w{player}: `$"{dFirst} would have loved {article} {item}. I didn't know {dHim}, but I feel it. ${price}."

`w{player}: `$"For just ${price}, {article} {item} will make the other mourners feel cheap. Isn't that what this is about?"

`w{player}: `$"We're running a special on {item}. It's ${price}. That's the special price. It's always the special price."

`w{player}: `$"You know what this funeral needs? {item}. ${price}. Don't ask me why, I just feel it."

`w{player}: `$"I shouldn't tell you this, but the mayor's mother had {article} {item}. ${price}."

`w{player}: `$"Grief is a journey, {cSir}, and every journey needs {article} {item}. ${price}."

`w{player}: `$"A lot of people regret not getting {article} {item}. For about a week. Then they forget. ${price}."

`w{player}: `$"I'd hate for you to wake up at 3 a.m. wishing you'd gotten {article} {item}. ${price}."

`w{player}: `$"The {item} is very popular this season. Death has seasons. ${price}."

`w{player}: `$"${price} for {article} {item}. Think of it as an investment in being talked about."

`w{player}: `$"Elijah at Di-Mart sells {article} {item} for half this. Elijah also sells bait. Ours is ${price} and has never touched a worm."

`w{player}: `$"The Blaine Funeral Home doesn't even offer {article} {item}. That's why Blaine is sad. ${price}."

`w{player}: `$"I'm legally required to tell you about {article} {item}. I'm not, but I like telling people. ${price}."

`w{player}: `$"{dFirst} can't take it with {dHim}. But {dHe} can take {article} {item}. ${price}."

`w{player}: `$"Father Smyth calls {article} {item} "the least you could do". Father Smyth is a very good customer. ${price}."

`w{player}: `$"Picture the wake. Everyone's talking about {dFirst}. Then someone whispers, "Is that {article} {item}?" ${price}."

`w{player}: `$"Our {item} comes with a lifetime guarantee. {dFirst}'s lifetime, so the paperwork is very simple. ${price}."

`w{player}: `$"I'll be honest with you, {cSir}. I'm not always honest. But {article} {item} for ${price} is a fair deal."

`w{player}: `$"Morty, my skeleton, recommends {article} {item}. He doesn't say much. He sort of leans. ${price}."

`w{player}: `$"Everyone at the service will want something to look at that isn't {dFirst}. Give them {article} {item}. ${price}."

`w{player}: `$"The {surname} name deserves {article} {item}. I don't know the {surname} name. It sounds deserving. ${price}."

`w{player}: `$"I could put {dHim} in wood. I could also put {dHim} in a trash bag. Silver is ${price} more and has handles."

`w{player}: `$"Do you want people whispering 'wood' at the viewing? Silver is ${price} more."

`w{player}: `$"Silver. ${price} more. Your {dRelation} survived {aFridge}, well, nearly. {dHeCap} deserves silver."

`w{player}: `$"Wood is what the silver caskets are shipped in. ${price} more and {dFirst} gets the casket instead of the crate."

`w{player}: `$"I'd go wood myself, but I'm a terrible person. You're not, are you? Silver is ${price} more."

`w{player}: `$"Silver caskets don't creak when the pallbearers lift them. Wood ones say things. Rude things. ${price} more."

`w{player}: `$"Our wood casket was put together by a man named Gary on his lunch break. Silver, ${price} more, was not Gary."

`w{player}: `$"Silver is ${price} more, and it doesn't look like something Elijah sells at Di-Mart next to the lawn furniture."

`w{player}: `$"When the {dFridge} got {dHim}, do you think {dHe} was hoping for wood next? Silver is ${price} more."

`w{player}: `$"Silver has a lining. Wood has a smell. ${price} difference."

`w{player}: `$"Woodpeckers. That's all I'll say. Silver, ${price} more."

`w{player}: `$"Wood is "rustic", which is the word we use for "cheap" when the family is in the room. Silver is ${price} more."

`w{player}: `$"Silver comes with a twenty-year warranty against worms. Wood comes with worms. ${price} more."

`w{player}: `$"Think of gold as first class. It's a one-way trip, so you might as well. ${price} more."

`w{player}: `$"Gold is what pharaohs got. {dFirst} wasn't a pharaoh, but {dHe} was {dSmashed} {aFridge}, which is nearly as rare. ${price} more."

`w{player}: `$"Look, you're already at silver. You can see gold from here. It's right there. ${price} more."

guiltPitch:
`w{player}: `$"{dFirst} would have done anything for you. And you're thinking about saving a few bucks?"

`w{player}: `$"I'm sure {dHe} would understand you going cheap. {dHeCap}'s dead, so {dHe} has to understand."

`w{player}: `$"People at the wake will look in that casket, {cSir}, and then they'll look at you."

`w{player}: `$"Some folks spend more on their cars than on their {dRelation}. You're not one of those folks, are you?"

`w{player}: `$"{dFirst} is watching from somewhere, {cSir}. Maybe heaven. Maybe the other place. But watching."

`w{player}: `$"What will you tell people? '{dFirst} got the discount box'?"

`w{player}: `$"You only bury your {dRelation} once. Usually."

`w{player}: `$"{dFirst} was lucky to have you. I can tell. You're the kind of person who reads the fine print and still cries."

`w{player}: `$"Tell me something {dFirst} used to say. Anything. Something stupid is fine. Those are the best ones."

tutorial.speaker: `wClerk: `$
pages:
`wClerk: `$"Welcome to Deathville, {name}! I'm from the Funeral Director's Guild. Congratulations on {parlor}. It's... a building. It has a door and most of its windows.

I'll walk you through your first day. Two minutes. Or press Skip and learn the hard way, like the last fellow. We buried him Tuesday."

`wClerk: `$"Every day you get turns. Each customer you meet costs one. Unused turns carry over to tomorrow, but only up to one day's worth, so sleeping in all week won't make you rich.

Every funeral earns Bury Points. Whoever has the most at the end of the season wins, and gets to be smug at the Guild picnic."

`wClerk: `$"Every customer has a limit: the most they'll spend. You never see it. You see an estimate, a range, and the real number is somewhere inside it. Not necessarily the middle. Psychology classes at Spirit University narrow it down.

Nothing you sell can push the bill past their limit. They'll just say no."

`wClerk: `$"Here's the trick. Land the bill within 8% of their limit and you get a bonus. Within 3%, a bigger one. Hit it to the dollar and the whole town reads about it in the paper.

Every price in this business is a multiple of fifty dollars, so the exact number can always be reached. In theory. In practice, people cry on the calculator."

`wClerk: `$"Watch their mood and their patience. Every pitch uses up a little patience. When it runs out, everything you do annoys them, and if they get angry enough they walk out and a rival gets the body.

What a customer says is true. Someone clutching a photo loved the deceased: use Sympathy. Someone watching the clock didn't: Guilt works. Listen costs two patience and teaches you something new."

`wClerk: `$"Soft Sell deals you a hand of three extras; pick one that fits under the top of the estimate. Packages upgrade the embalming, flowers, plot, headstone and service, one step at a time. Hard Sell moves them up a casket.

Coffee calms someone down, once per customer. A Discount takes a little off the bill and cheers them up, twice at most. Press Done when the bill is where you want it."

`wClerk: `$"After some funerals you'll prepare the body yourself, and there'll be a choice. A ring left on a finger. A fat wallet. Take it, or leave it.

That's karma. Be good and the town trusts you: calmer, richer customers. Be bad and the money's nice, the hours are flexible, and the Guild pretends it doesn't know you."

`wClerk: `$"Cash is for the business. Di-Mart sells caskets wholesale; ask for Elijah, and don't let him touch your hair. Selling from stock pays better than a rush order. Your office has upgrades: paint, a coffee machine, one day a chapel.

That's it! Your first customer is waiting. I'll be watching. Taking notes. Don't mind me."

hints.hand: Clerk: Pick the card that brings the bill closest to their limit without going over.
hints.packages: Clerk: Each card upgrades one part of the funeral by one step. Mind the price.
hints.afterPitch: Clerk: Watch the mood and the patience. When the bill is near the top of the estimate, press Done.
hints.impatient: Clerk: They're out of patience! Everything you do now makes them angrier. Wrap it up.
hints.done: Clerk: Not bad at all. Press Continue. I'm writing 'not bad at all' in my little book.

tutorial.finish: `wClerk: `$"Not bad for a first day! Wait for customers until your turns run out, then see the town: Di-Mart for caskets, your office for upgrades, Spirit University if you'd like to read minds. Good luck. Try not to get stabbed."

beats.headline: LIGHTNING SPLITS ST. MORTIMER'S STEEPLE
beats.story: Father Smyth blames the lightning; the lightning has no comment. The church needs money for repairs. Reaper Club owner Lucius Vane has offered to buy the lot for a parking garage. "People die in parking garages all the time," said Vane. "Everybody wins." Give at the church or at the club. The bigger pile decides within the week.

appeals.label: Give to the Steeple Fund
appeals.thanks: `$Father Smyth counts your `w${money}`$ twice and blesses you once. The second count was the blessing.

appeals.label: Chip In for the Bulldozer
appeals.thanks: `$Lucius Vane pockets your `w${money}`$ and calls you "partner." Nobody has ever called you partner before.

beats.headline: VANE DOUBLES BID; SMYTH DOUBLES SERMON
beats.story: Vane has doubled his offer and thrown in free parking for the funerals of anyone who sells to him. Father Smyth preached for ninety minutes on the money changers in the temple, then passed the plate twice. Old Man Withers has chained himself to the font, though he says he only sat down and got stuck.

appeals.label: Pass the Plate Again
appeals.thanks: `$The plate comes round a second time. Your `w${money}`$ lands with a thud and Father Smyth winks at the ceiling.

appeals.label: Buy Vane a Bigger Bulldozer
appeals.thanks: `$Vane folds your `w${money}`$ into his breast pocket. "Bigger blade, smaller church. That's arithmetic."

beats.headline: BELLS RING AGAIN OVER DEATHVILLE
beats.story: The steeple is back, a foot taller than before out of spite. The town is calmer for it, and the bells now ring twice for every funeral. {top} gave the most and gets a brass plaque by the door that nobody will read.

beats.headline: ST. MORTIMER'S IS NOW LEVEL 2, ROW C
beats.story: The bulldozers came at dawn. Bingo is cancelled until somebody finds the cards under the rubble. The Reaper Club is celebrating with cheap cover. Father Smyth is holding services in Space 14 and says the acoustics are "honestly better."

beats.headline: MYSTERY COUGH SWEEPS DEATHVILLE
beats.story: The coroner calls it "a cough with ambitions." Business is booming and the families are frantic. If too many of them storm out of our parlors, the papers say, they'll take their dead to Bigtown. A clinic fund is open at City Hall.

appeals.label: Fund the Cough Clinic
appeals.thanks: `$The Mayor's office takes your `w${money}`$. A clinic will be built, or at the very least discussed at length.

appeals.label: Light a Candle for the Sick
appeals.thanks: `$You buy a candle for `w${money}`$. It is a very expensive candle. Father Smyth says the money goes to the clinic.

beats.headline: COUGH WARD FULL; NURSE 'RUNNING ON COFFEE AND SPITE'
beats.story: "Keep your hands washed and your parlors open," says Nurse Gertie, who has slept four hours this week. Families with a cough and a body are lining up at every door in town. The Bigtown parlors have started advertising on our radio station.

appeals.label: Fund the Cough Clinic
appeals.thanks: `$The Mayor's office takes your `w${money}`$. A clinic will be built, or at the very least discussed at length.

appeals.label: Light a Candle for the Sick
appeals.thanks: `$You buy a candle for `w${money}`$. It is a very expensive candle. Father Smyth says the money goes to the clinic.

beats.headline: FAMILIES FLEE TO BIGTOWN FOR FUNERALS
beats.story: "At least in Bigtown the undertakers don't throw you out," said one mourner, loading grandma into a station wagon. Deathville's morticians will be poorer for a week, and Bigtown has sent a thank-you card.

beats.headline: DEATHVILLE'S MORTICIANS HAILED AS HEROES
beats.story: Not one grieving family turned away, or not many. The cough is passing, and families are paying a little extra out of gratitude. The clinic's donors will be mentioned at every funeral this week, briefly.

beats.headline: MAYOR TAKES CREDIT FOR CURE
beats.story: At a press conference {mayor} thanked "the brave morticians, and also me, mostly me." Every parlor in town got a certificate. {mayor} got a parade, and rode in it twice.

beats.headline: TOWN ERECTS STATUE OF THE UNKNOWN UNDERTAKER
beats.story: With nobody elected to take the credit, the town gave it to all of you: a statue in the square of a man in a black suit holding out his hand, palm up. It stands next to the Mayor's statues, which it outranks.

beats.headline: MORTY THE SKELETON FILES AS WRITE-IN CANDIDATE
beats.story: A petition with 212 signatures, most of them from the cemetery, has put Morty on the ballot. His platform is "Bones." His campaign manager, who gave his name only as Cousin Sal, promises to "cut taxes to the bone." Volunteers sign up at City Hall. The smart money at the Reaper Club is against him.

appeals.label: Volunteer for Morty's Campaign
appeals.thanks: `$A volunteer staples a MORTY: HE'LL NEVER LEAVE YOU sign to your hearse. Your `w${money}`$ buys a great many staples.

appeals.label: Bet Against the Skeleton
appeals.thanks: `$Lucius Vane writes your `w${money}`$ in a little black book. "Skeletons never win. They don't have the stomach for it."

beats.headline: MORTY SAYS NOTHING FOR NINETY MINUTES, WINS DEBATE
beats.story: At the candidates' forum Morty said nothing at all, which voters called "refreshing" and "the best speech in years." A heckler threw a tomato. It went straight through him. The count is days away.

appeals.label: Volunteer for Morty's Campaign
appeals.thanks: `$A volunteer staples a MORTY: HE'LL NEVER LEAVE YOU sign to your hearse. Your `w${money}`$ buys a great many staples.

appeals.label: Bet Against the Skeleton
appeals.thanks: `$Lucius Vane writes your `w${money}`$ in a little black book. "Skeletons never win. They don't have the stomach for it."

beats.headline: MORTY CONCEDES: 'I HAD NO BODY BEHIND ME'
beats.story: {mayor} won the count fair and square, or close enough. Morty conceded with dignity, mostly by falling over. The new mayor has given him a job in the City Hall lobby, holding the door, which he does very well.

beats.headline: NOBODY RAN, SO MORTY WON
beats.story: With no living candidate on the ballot, Morty was declared Honorary Mayor. He will cut ribbons and stand in the corner of the council chamber. {mayor} stays in charge of anything that matters and says he is "honestly relieved." The town is in an unusually good mood.

arcs.title: The Grave Robber of Row C

beats.headline: SOMEBODY IS DIGGING UP ROW C
beats.story: Eleven graves were opened this week, and every one lost its jewelry and its dignity. The groundskeeper blames raccoons. The raccoons blame each other. Father Smyth is raising money for a night watchman. The Reaper Club is selling maps.

appeals.label: Pay for a Night Watchman
appeals.thanks: `$Father Smyth takes your `w${money}`$ for the watchman. "A good man, with a lantern and a very short temper."

appeals.label: Buy a Map of Row C
appeals.thanks: `$A man in a trench coat swaps your `w${money}`$ for a map drawn on a napkin. The X is in ketchup.

beats.headline: GRAVEYARD DOG FOUND WEARING A DEAD WOMAN'S RING
beats.story: The ring belonged to Mrs. Hubble, Row C, Plot 9. Deacon will not say where he got it, and the groundskeeper will not say where Deacon has been sleeping. Nobody has been arrested. Several people have been sniffed.

appeals.label: Pay for a Night Watchman
appeals.thanks: `$Father Smyth takes your `w${money}`$ for the watchman. "A good man, with a lantern and a very short temper."

appeals.label: Buy a Map of Row C
appeals.thanks: `$A man in a trench coat swaps your `w${money}`$ for a map drawn on a napkin. The X is in ketchup.

beats.headline: GRAVE ROBBER CAUGHT: IT WAS A RACCOON IN A HAT
beats.story: The church's night watchman caught the culprit red-handed: a raccoon in a tiny hat, with a tiny shovel. Police suspect "a human mastermind." {top} paid for most of the watchman and gets a bench with their name on it. The raccoon sleeps on it.

beats.headline: ROW C EMPTIED; MOURNERS ASK 'WHERE IS GRANDPA?'
beats.story: By Friday there was nothing in Row C but holes and a raccoon in a hat. Families are visiting the Reaper Club to ask who sold the maps. Lucius Vane says he has never seen a map, and that the ketchup is not his.

beats.headline: DI-MART ANNOUNCES ITS NINTH 'FINAL CLEARANCE'
beats.story: Head office will close the Deathville store for good unless it moves more merchandise this week. Elijah, asked how he feels, stared at our reporter until he left. Caskets are ten percent off. If the town's undertakers sell enough funerals this week, they will save Elijah's job, whether they wanted to or not.

appeals.label: Sign the Save Elijah Petition
appeals.thanks: `$You sign, and your `w${money}`$ goes to the Friends of Elijah. The Friends of Elijah is one woman with a clipboard.

appeals.label: Bet on Di-Mart Closing
appeals.thanks: `$Vane takes your `w${money}`$ at four to one. "Nothing lasts forever," he says. "Except that clerk."

beats.headline: DI-MART HEAD OFFICE SENDS A MAN WITH A CLIPBOARD
beats.story: The man with the clipboard counted every casket in the store, then counted them again, then asked Elijah how long he had worked there. Elijah answered "yes." The clipboard man has extended the sale and is watching the town's sales figures very closely.

appeals.label: Sign the Save Elijah Petition
appeals.thanks: `$You sign, and your `w${money}`$ goes to the Friends of Elijah. The Friends of Elijah is one woman with a clipboard.

appeals.label: Bet on Di-Mart Closing
appeals.thanks: `$Vane takes your `w${money}`$ at four to one. "Nothing lasts forever," he says. "Except that clerk."

beats.headline: DI-MART SAVED; ELIJAH NAMED EMPLOYEE OF THE CENTURY
beats.story: The town's undertakers sold enough funerals to keep the store open. Head office gave Elijah a plaque, a pin and a staff discount, which he has passed on to "my friends, the undertakers." He did not blink once during the ceremony.

beats.headline: DI-MART CLOSES FOREVER, REOPENS AN HOUR LATER
beats.story: Head office shut the store at nine and sold it at ten, to a holding company whose only employee is Elijah. Prices are up "to cover the paperwork." Elijah was at the register when the doors reopened. Nobody saw him leave.

beats.headline: THE TWINS BUY ALL THE LIGHTER FLUID IN THE COUNTY
beats.story: Hardware stores in three towns say the Twins bought every can, paid in singed bills and asked whether it came in "extra." The volunteer fire brigade has one truck, no hose and a dalmatian named Captain. A hose fund is open at the church. The Twins drink at the Reaper Club, where people are buying them rounds.

appeals.label: Buy the Fire Brigade a Hose
appeals.thanks: `$Your `w${money}`$ goes in a coffee can marked HOSE. The brigade's dalmatian licks your hand in thanks, then your face.

appeals.label: Buy the Twins a Round
appeals.thanks: `$The Twins raise their glasses at the same moment. "To warmth," they say. Your `w${money}`$ was spent on something flammable.

beats.headline: TWINS ANNOUNCE 'BIRDHOUSE FESTIVAL' ON ELM STREET
beats.story: Every house on Elm Street will get a free birdhouse, hand-made by the Twins and filled, they say, "with a surprise." The fire brigade has asked residents not to open the surprise. Asked what the surprise is, the Twins answered at exactly the same time: "Warmth."

appeals.label: Buy the Fire Brigade a Hose
appeals.thanks: `$Your `w${money}`$ goes in a coffee can marked HOSE. The brigade's dalmatian licks your hand in thanks, then your face.

appeals.label: Buy the Twins a Round
appeals.thanks: `$The Twins raise their glasses at the same moment. "To warmth," they say. Your `w${money}`$ was spent on something flammable.

beats.headline: FIRE BRIGADE GETS A HOSE; TWINS GET BORED
beats.story: With a new hose and the dalmatian on alert, the Birdhouse Festival fizzled. The Twins left for Blaine "for a change of scenery." Elm Street is quiet, safe and slightly damp. {top} paid for most of the hose and is now an honorary firefighter, with a hat.

beats.headline: ELM STREET BIRDHOUSE FESTIVAL ENDS AS YOU'D EXPECT
beats.story: The surprise was warmth. Elm Street burned end to end while the brigade looked for a hose it never got. Nobody was badly hurt except, it turns out, quite a few people, all of them well insured. The Twins have sent every parlor in town a thank-you card.

arcs.title: Old Man Withers Picks a Day

beats.headline: OLD MAN WITHERS ANNOUNCES DEATH FOR SATURDAY
beats.story: "I've decided," said Withers, 83, at bingo. "Saturday, after lunch." He has asked every parlor in town for a quote and the church to plan a wake. The Reaper Club has opened a pool on the hour. Withers has bought a ticket in the pool.

appeals.label: Chip In for Withers' Wake
appeals.thanks: `$Father Smyth puts your `w${money}`$ toward the wake. "Ham, potato salad, and a cake shaped like Withers. He asked for the cake."

appeals.label: Bet on the Hour He Goes
appeals.thanks: `$You put `w${money}`$ on Saturday at 3 p.m. The board behind the bar is full. Somebody has bet on 2047.

beats.headline: WITHERS UPDATE: STILL ALIVE, ORDERS SECONDS
beats.story: Saturday came. Withers ate lunch, then another lunch, then fell asleep in the bingo hall and woke shouting BINGO. Doctors say he has "the heart of a man half his age and the liver of a much braver man." The pool at the Reaper Club is now very large.

appeals.label: Chip In for Withers' Wake
appeals.thanks: `$Father Smyth puts your `w${money}`$ toward the wake. "Ham, potato salad, and a cake shaped like Withers. He asked for the cake."

appeals.label: Bet on the Hour He Goes
appeals.thanks: `$You put `w${money}`$ on Saturday at 3 p.m. The board behind the bar is full. Somebody has bet on 2047.

beats.headline: WITHERS WINS OWN DEATH POOL BY NOT DYING
beats.story: House rules said the pool goes to "whoever is closest," and Withers argued, successfully, that he was closest to himself. He collected every dollar, bought a new hearse and parks it outside the Reaper Club "so nobody has to call anyone later." Everyone who bet feels a little cursed.

beats.headline: WITHERS' LIVING WAKE IS THE PARTY OF THE YEAR
beats.story: The church held the wake anyway, with Withers in the front row criticizing the catering. He gave his own eulogy, which ran long, and heckled it. The whole town came, and left in a generous mood. Withers says the cake was "dry, but I'll allow it."

beats.headline: SOLEMNCORP EYES DEATHVILLE: 'A MARKET RIPE FOR DYING'
beats.story: The Bigtown funeral chain SolemnCorp, which runs 400 parlors from one call center, wants to open on Elm Street. "We bring big-city grief to small towns," says a regional manager with very white teeth. A Buy Local, Die Local fund is collecting at City Hall. SolemnCorp is quietly buying mailing lists at the Reaper Club.

appeals.label: Fund Buy Local, Die Local
appeals.thanks: `$Your `w${money}`$ prints a thousand bumper stickers: DIE LOCAL. Some people are taking it as an instruction.

appeals.label: Sell SolemnCorp a Mailing List
appeals.thanks: `$A man with very white teeth takes your list and a `w${money}`$ "processing fee," and calls it synergy. You feel processed.

beats.headline: TOWN MEETING ON SOLEMNCORP ENDS IN SHOUTING, SANDWICHES
beats.story: Two hundred residents packed City Hall. The SolemnCorp man gave a slide show called Grief, Simplified. Father Smyth called it "the work of the devil, but with charts." The council decides in two days.

appeals.label: Fund Buy Local, Die Local
appeals.thanks: `$Your `w${money}`$ prints a thousand bumper stickers: DIE LOCAL. Some people are taking it as an instruction.

appeals.label: Sell SolemnCorp a Mailing List
appeals.thanks: `$A man with very white teeth takes your list and a `w${money}`$ "processing fee," and calls it synergy. You feel processed.

beats.headline: SOLEMNCORP PULLS OUT: 'TOO MUCH LOCAL CHARACTER'
beats.story: The council turned SolemnCorp down flat, and the man with the teeth drove back to Bigtown with his slide show. {top}'s face is on the DIE LOCAL poster in the City Hall window. Families are proud to bury their own this week.

beats.headline: SOLEMNCORP OPENS ON ELM STREET; FREE BALLOONS
beats.story: The new branch has a drive-through, a loyalty card and balloons that say SORRY. Families are trying it, and coming back to haggle with what they learned. "If Deathville's families keep walking out on local parlors," says the man with the teeth, "we'll be here to catch them."

beats.headline: SOLEMNCORP BUYS THE CEMETERY
beats.story: "Deathville's families kept walking out of their parlors, so we gave them somewhere to walk to," says the man with the teeth, who has also bought the cemetery's mowing contract, and then the cemetery. Plot rents now go to Bigtown first.

beats.headline: SOLEMNCORP GOES BUST; CALL CENTER STILL RINGING
beats.story: Hardly a family walked out of a local parlor, so SolemnCorp had nobody to sign. The Elm Street branch closed with the balloons still up. The call center in Bigtown is still answering the phone, and is still very sorry for your loss.

beats.headline: NURSE GERTIE TO RETIRE; COUSIN SAL APPLIES
beats.story: "Thirty-one years, prince, and they still won't let me smoke in the morgue," said Nurse Gertie, giving notice. The hospital board picks her replacement this week. The only applicant is Cousin Sal, M.D. (University of P.O. Box 411). A fund to keep Gertie is open at City Hall. Sal's campaign runs from a booth at the Reaper Club.

appeals.label: Fund the Nurse's Raise
appeals.thanks: `$The hospital board takes your `w${money}`$. Nurse Gertie hears about it by lunch. "You're a prince, prince."

appeals.label: Buy Cousin Sal a Stethoscope
appeals.thanks: `$Sal tries the stethoscope on your `w${money}`$ and says it has a strong pulse. He puts the money in his sock.

beats.headline: SAL'S INTERVIEW: 'WHERE DO YOU KEEP THE GOOD STUFF?'
beats.story: Board members describe Cousin Sal's interview as "short" and "mostly questions from him." His references are all in the same handwriting. Gertie has been seen at the travel agent, asking about cruises "with a good infirmary."

appeals.label: Fund the Nurse's Raise
appeals.thanks: `$The hospital board takes your `w${money}`$. Nurse Gertie hears about it by lunch. "You're a prince, prince."

appeals.label: Buy Cousin Sal a Stethoscope
appeals.thanks: `$Sal tries the stethoscope on your `w${money}`$ and says it has a strong pulse. He puts the money in his sock.

beats.headline: GERTIE STAYS ON: 'SOMEBODY HAS TO KEEP SAL OUT'
beats.story: Nurse Gertie cancelled the cruise and framed her raise, which she says is "smaller than the frame." Treatment is cheaper this week "because I'm in a mood, prince." {top} gave the most and gets a free tetanus shot, whether they want it or not.

beats.headline: COUSIN SAL NAMED HEAD NURSE
beats.story: "Prices are down, patients are down, everything's down," said Sal, in a white coat with somebody else's name on it. Discharges are up three hundred percent, mostly through the back door. Gertie is working nights anyway, "to count them."

beats.headline: LAKE BLEAK MONSTER SPOTTED FROM TOWN BEACH
beats.story: Forty bathers watched a long green shape cross the lake at lunchtime and burp. County scientists want a grant to study it "gently." Lucius Vane is outfitting a hunting party with harpoons, a rowboat and a cooler. Science collects at City Hall; the hunt collects at the Reaper Club.

appeals.label: Fund the Monster Study
appeals.thanks: `$Your `w${money}`$ buys the county scientists a canoe and a notebook. "We'll be very gentle," they promise. The canoe is not very gentle.

appeals.label: Buy a Harpoon for Vane's Hunt
appeals.thanks: `$Vane hands you a harpoon with your name on it for `w${money}`$. "You don't have to come," he says. "It's more of a donation with a point."

beats.headline: TWO FISHERMEN MISSING; MONSTER 'NOT HUNGRY ANYMORE'
beats.story: Their boat came back without them, and with a burp. The parks department has put up a sign that says PLEASE DO NOT FEED THE LAKE. Lake-house families are calling the parlors, and the scientists and the hunters are both asking for more money.

appeals.label: Fund the Monster Study
appeals.thanks: `$Your `w${money}`$ buys the county scientists a canoe and a notebook. "We'll be very gentle," they promise. The canoe is not very gentle.

appeals.label: Buy a Harpoon for Vane's Hunt
appeals.thanks: `$Vane hands you a harpoon with your name on it for `w${money}`$. "You don't have to come," he says. "It's more of a donation with a point."

beats.headline: HUNTERS HARPOON LAKE MONSTER; IT WAS THE OLD FERRY
beats.story: Vane's party rowed out at dawn, harpooned a long green shape in the reeds and towed it in to cheers. It was the Lake Bleak ferry, missing since 1974, and the passengers were all still aboard. Every parlor in town is busy, and Vane is calling it a success.

beats.headline: SCIENTISTS: MONSTER IS 'SHY, LONELY, AND ABOUT FORTY FEET'
beats.story: The county study found the creature eats mostly carp, the odd speedboat and, once, a tax assessor, which nobody is pursuing. Tourists are arriving by the busload, some of them in swimsuits, all of them with money.

beats.headline: FENWICK DEMANDS NO-CONFIDENCE VOTE AT CITY HALL
beats.story: Doris Fenwick, retired dentist, has filed a motion of no confidence in {mayor}, citing "the statues, the potholes, and the statues." Signatures are being taken at City Hall. The Mayor's defense fund has a booth at the Reaper Club "for supporters with discretion."

appeals.label: Sign Fenwick's Petition
appeals.thanks: `$Doris Fenwick shakes your hand, takes your `w${money}`$ and checks your gums. "Floss more," she says. "And vote."

appeals.label: Donate to the Mayor's Legal Fund
appeals.thanks: `$A man from the Mayor's office takes your `w${money}`$ in a paper bag. He gives you a lapel pin of a statue.

beats.headline: NO-CONFIDENCE HEARING: MAYOR'S OFFICE ENTERS STATUE AS EVIDENCE
beats.story: {mayor} told the council that "confidence is a feeling, and feelings are not in the town charter." Fenwick brought charts. The council votes in two days, after a great many free lunches.

appeals.label: Sign Fenwick's Petition
appeals.thanks: `$Doris Fenwick shakes your hand, takes your `w${money}`$ and checks your gums. "Floss more," she says. "And vote."

appeals.label: Donate to the Mayor's Legal Fund
appeals.thanks: `$A man from the Mayor's office takes your `w${money}`$ in a paper bag. He gives you a lapel pin of a statue.

beats.headline: COUNCIL VOTES NO CONFIDENCE; NOTHING HAPPENS
beats.story: By four votes to one the council declared it has no confidence in {mayor}. The vote is symbolic, so {mayor} stays in office without any, which the Mayor's office says is "how most people live." As a consolation the permit office is to be audited, which has frightened it into lowering prices.

beats.headline: MAYOR SURVIVES NO-CONFIDENCE VOTE, UNVEILS STATUE OF SURVIVAL
beats.story: The motion failed four votes to one; Fenwick's was the one. {mayor} celebrated with a fourth statue, paid for by "a small increase in permit fees and a large one in morale." Fenwick has announced she will run again, for everything.

injuries.name: Dog Bite
injuries.text: `$Deacon, the groundskeeper's dog, took a piece of you and buried it somewhere. You will never see it again.

injuries.name: Sprained Ankle
injuries.text: `$You stepped into an open grave mid-swing. The occupant was very understanding about it, being dead.

injuries.name: Cracked Skull
injuries.text: `$Something cracked. You hope it was a walnut. You were not carrying a walnut.

injuries.name: Pickled Liver
injuries.text: `$That was not vodka. Your liver is now legally a specimen and will outlive you in a jar.

injuries.name: Busted Kneecaps
injuries.text: `$Two men with a tire iron explained a few things to your knees. Your knees understood right away.

injuries.name: Shovel-Shaped Face
injuries.text: `$Something flat and heavy met your face. The imprint is shovel-shaped, and perfect. Customers keep asking where you had it done.

injuries.name: Broken Toe (Granite)
injuries.text: `$You kicked a headstone for emphasis. It was granite. You now walk like Old Man Withers, but slower.

injuries.name: Lily Rash
injuries.text: `$You landed face first in the funeral lilies. You are allergic to lilies. You are now mostly rash.

injuries.name: Embalmed Thumb
injuries.text: `$You stuck yourself with the trocar. Your thumb is preserved for the ages and will never bend again.

injuries.name: Thrown-Out Back
injuries.text: `$Somebody threw you over a shoulder like a sack of flour. Your back went out and has not called.

injuries.name: Bingo Elbow
injuries.text: `$Old Man Withers elbowed you on his way to the front row. He is eighty-three and he is mostly elbow.

injuries.name: Rib Splinter
injuries.text: `$Morty fell on you. You have a splinter of rib in your arm. Morty is one rib short and won't discuss it.

injuries.name: Gold Tag Paper Cut
injuries.text: `$A gold casket tag sliced your finger. It is the most expensive cut in town and it knows it.

injuries.name: Formaldehyde Eyes
injuries.text: `$Embalming fluid in both eyes. Everything looks peaceful, slightly yellow and very far away.

injuries.name: Lectern Lump
injuries.text: `$You leaned on the eulogy lectern and it gave way. The Lord took the lectern's side.

injuries.name: Bouncer's Handprint
injuries.text: `$The Reaper Club's bouncer helped you out the door by the neck. You can still feel every finger. All six.

market.name: Rabbit's Foot (Still Twitching)
market.text: Lucky for you. Less lucky for the rabbit, who is around here somewhere on three legs, looking for you.

market.name: Bulletproof Vest, One Small Hole
market.text: Stops the next injury. The previous owner swears it works. You can ask him at the cemetery.

market.name: Gold Casket That Fell Off a Truck
market.text: Half Di-Mart's price. Don't ask whose truck. It goes in your storeroom and you never saw the man.

market.name: The Coroner's Morning List
market.text: Names, addresses, time of death. One sure customer, if you knock first and wipe your feet.

market.name: Forged Permit
market.text: The cheapest City Hall permit you don't have, signed by a mayor who may not exist.

market.name: A Gold Tag, Numbers Filed Off
market.text: One gold casket tag. It came off somebody's casket. Possibly with them still in it.

market.name: Holy Water (Tap)
market.text: One bottle, filled at the club's sink. It's as holy as you believe it is. Bless a customer with it.

market.name: A Large Man Named Tiny
market.text: Sleeps on your porch tonight. Nobody gets past Tiny. Tiny gets past everybody, including the porch.

market.name: Morty's Spare Rib
market.text: Sold as lucky. The man swears it's Morty's. You count Morty's ribs when you get home. He's short two.

market.name: A Policeman's Day Off
market.text: Officer Dunn parks outside your parlor all night and arrests anyone who tries the door. He's on vacation.

market.name: Five-Star Testimonials, Handwritten
market.text: Glowing reviews from very satisfied customers, in a very shaky hand. The customers can't object.

market.name: Four-Leaf Clover From a Fresh Grave
market.text: It grew out of somebody. That's what makes it lucky. That's also what makes it smell.

market.name: Holy Water (The Real Stuff)
market.text: Taken from St. Mortimer's font by a man who crossed himself the whole time. It's genuine. That's the problem.

market.name: Cousin Sal's Prescription Pad
market.text: Sal writes one patient a prescription. Two days later they need you. Sal calls it a referral network.

market.name: A Hearse-Full of Wreaths (Used Once)
market.text: Lifted off yesterday's graves before the mourners reached their cars. Families will say you went all out.

market.name: Riot Shield From the Police Strike
market.text: It says POLICE on it. Stops the next injury. Nobody has asked for it back and nobody will.

market.name: The Twins' Cousin, Bruno
market.text: Sleeps in your hearse tonight with a crowbar and a hip flask. He's related to the Twins by nothing you can prove.

market.name: A Gold Casket, Lightly Haunted
market.text: Cheaper than the one off the truck because it comes with a previous owner. He's quiet. Mostly. At night, no.

market.name: The Mayor's Spare Key
market.text: Opens the permit cabinet at City Hall. Take the next permit you need and stamp it. The stamp says GRUBB.

market.name: Lake Bleak Monster Scale
market.text: Green, the size of a dinner plate, sold as proof. Rub it for luck. Do not rub it anywhere near the lake.

monuments: A Granite Bench With Your Name on the Seat
A Marble Obelisk You Can See From Blaine
A Bronze Statue of You, One Foot Taller Than the Mayor's

news.title: SHAKEUP IN DEATHVILLE
news.message: A small earthquake rattled the town at dawn. Some casualties. "I barely felt it, actually," said the Mayor, from under his desk, where he has been since Tuesday for unrelated reasons.
news.effect: +1 turn today, more customers, fewer distractions

news.title: MORTUARIES DO ROCKIN' BUSINESS
news.message: The big one hit downtown. "I'm glad we have so many funeral parlors in this town. We're gonna need 'em today," said a man pinned under the Di-Mart sign, who then asked for a price list. Di-Mart has marked everything up "for structural reasons".
news.effect: +2 turns today, families spend 10% more, Di-Mart caskets 10% dearer

news.title: DEATH WITH DIGNITY, NOW 20 PERCENT OFF
news.message: "For a comfortable eternal lay, come see us today!" says the Di-Mart flyer. Elijah will be at the register. Elijah was at the register when they built the store around him.

news.title: BILL'S BIG BURGER: NOW WITH E. COLI
news.message: An outbreak at Bill's Big Burger has left many dead and many more just puking a lot. "We stand by the meat," said Bill, who has never eaten there. The ones still puking are in a mood.

news.title: SPEED LIMIT RAISED, PEDESTRIANS LOWERED
news.message: Elm Street is now a 65 zone. "We should have known people can't dodge cars," admits the Department of Transportation, whose own van was hit twice before lunch. Families are arriving in a hurry and in pieces.

news.title: ZOO EMPTIES OVERNIGHT; DIRECTOR BLAMES 'OPEN-DOOR POLICY'
news.message: Everything at Deathville Zoo got out, led by the "mostly tame" tiger. "Now their rage is out of the cage," says director Hank Pruitt, from a tree. The animals are seeking revenge on humans and cotton candy.

news.title: THIRTY MINUTES OR YOUR LIFE
news.message: Bad cheese at Crusty Carl's Pizza. "If they didn't eat it in under thirty minutes they would die, and if they did, they also died," reports some dude. Guilty families are paying for nice funerals.

news.title: MARKET CRASH: BANKERS JUMP, DON'T TIP
news.message: Stocks fell forty percent overnight, and so did several investors, from the roof of Deathville Savings. Teller Prudence Ledbetter says she "saw it coming" and "didn't think it was her place." Di-Mart is dumping inventory.

news.title: LOCAL MAN WINS LOTTERY, DIES OF EXCITEMENT
news.message: His family is rich now, and so are their friends, who all seem to be dropping dead in sympathy. The lottery office now asks winners to sit down, and to pre-plan, before checking their numbers.

news.title: POLICE ON STRIKE
news.message: "We want dental," says the Police Commissioner. Crime is up. Morticians are settling old scores, and the graveyard keeper has locked himself in the tool shed with Deacon and a ham.
news.effect: fights pay 20% more, grave robbers +10 luck

news.title: HEAT WAVE: THE DEAD WON'T KEEP
news.message: "Get them in the ground by lunch or you'll smell them by dinner," warns the county coroner, who has moved his office into the Di-Mart freezer aisle, next to the fish sticks.
news.effect: more bodies to prepare, customers 1 patience shorter

news.title: ST. MORTIMER'S BINGO GOES CUT-FREE FOR SAINT'S DAY
news.message: Father Smyth has waived the church's cut for one night "in honour of a saint I am fairly sure exists." Old Man Withers has been camped on the steps since four with a folding chair and eleven daubers.
news.effect: tonight's bingo pays the whole pot

news.title: BINGO CANCELLED AFTER WITHERS CALLS IT TWICE
news.message: Old Man Withers shouted BINGO on the third number, again on the fourth, then fell asleep on the cards. Father Smyth has cancelled tonight "to pray, and to look at smaller halls." The town is oddly relaxed.
news.effect: no bingo tonight, customers a little calmer

news.title: HOSPITAL CLEARANCE: 'EVERYTHING MUST GO'
news.message: Nurse Gertie says the hospital is "clearing old stock" and will set any bone in town at half price. "Bring a friend, prince. Bring two. Bring whatever's left of them."

news.title: ORDERLIES WALK OUT; NURSE RUNS HOSPITAL WITH A STAPLER
news.message: "Nobody leaves until they're fixed or finished," says Nurse Gertie. So far it is mostly finished. The billing department, which did not strike, has raised its prices to cover the stapler.
news.effect: hospital 50% dearer, more bodies to prepare

news.title: DEATHVILLE SAVINGS RAISES RATES, TELLER RAISES ONE EYEBROW
news.message: "We are rewarding thrift," said the bank's spokesman, Prudence Ledbetter, who is also its teller, its guard and its Employee of the Month. She then said "don't get excited" and closed the window.
news.effect: savings +0.2% tonight, loans 1% a day dearer

news.title: BANK DECLARES WAR ON COUSIN SAL'S LENDING
news.message: Deathville Savings has cut its loan rate to compete with Cousin Sal, who lends from the trunk of a station wagon. "Sal doesn't have a vault," the teller points out. "Sal has a tire iron."

news.title: CITY HALL CLERK WAKES UP, APPROVES EVERYTHING
news.message: The permit clerk woke for the first time since spring and stamped every form in the building before anyone could stop him, including a lunch menu and a dog. Permits are half price while he's conscious.
news.effect: City Hall permits half price today

news.title: CONTRACTORS HOLD 'GOING OUT OF BUSINESS' SALE, AGAIN
news.message: "Fourth time this year," says the union rep. "We keep not going out of business. It's embarrassing." Everything with a hammer is ten percent off, and so is the hammer.

news.title: LUMBER SHORTAGE: CASKETS NOW 'MORE COMPACT'
news.message: "Pine is up, oak is up, and the man who sold us particleboard is in prison," says Di-Mart's buyer. Elijah has started measuring customers for "something more upright." Contractors charge extra to look at a nail.
news.effect: Di-Mart caskets and parlor upgrades 10% dearer

news.title: POLICE RAID REAPER CLUB, FIND ONLY MORTICIANS
news.message: Officers searched the Reaper Club top to bottom and found nothing illegal but the music. Lucius Vane is waiving a tag off the cover "for everyone who didn't talk." Certain services at the back are lying low.
news.effect: Reaper Club cover 1 tag cheaper, hit men 20% dearer

news.title: COUNTY RELEASES SIX MEN WITH TIRE IRONS, SAME DAY
news.message: A paperwork error at the county lock-up let six career kneecappers out on one morning. "Supply and demand," shrugs a man in a trench coat outside the Reaper Club. "Mostly supply."

news.title: GRAVEYARD DOG ON VACATION
news.message: Deacon, the cemetery's dog, is visiting his sister in Blaine. The groundskeeper says the graveyard is "as safe as ever," then asked reporters not to print that he is also at his sister's.

news.title: GRAVEYARD CLOSED FOR RE-SODDING
news.message: The parks department has closed the cemetery to "everything but the deceased" while it lays new turf over the bad patches. Some of the bad patches are moving. A man with a rake is guarding the gate.
news.effect: no graveyard duels today, grave robbers -10 luck

news.title: LOCAL PARLOR STARS IN 'GRAVE EXPECTATIONS'
news.message: A cable crew filmed one of our parlors for a reality show. It aired at 3 a.m. and everyone watched it anyway. Now every family wants a funeral "like on TV," and they clap at the end.

news.title: EXPOSED: WHAT YOUR UNDERTAKER ISN'T TELLING YOU
news.message: A Funeral Times investigation finds that local undertakers "charge too much, smile too much and own a suspicious number of shovels." Readers are shopping around today, and reading the small print out loud.
news.effect: customers haggle harder, sales earn 10% less BP

news.title: WIDOWS' SUPPORT GROUP LEARNS TO CRY ON CUE
news.message: "It works at the bank, at the car dealer and at the funeral home," says the group's leader, dabbing an eye that is completely dry. Undertakers report record sympathy, and record tissue sales.

news.title: CEMETERY PLOT VALUES DOUBLE OVERNIGHT
news.message: A rumour that Blaine is "running out of ground" has sent buyers our way. "It's the same dirt," says the county assessor, "but the view of Blaine is better from in here."

news.title: SINKHOLE SWALLOWS ROW F
news.message: Thirty graves dropped another six feet overnight. "They were six feet down already, so technically they're fine," says the parks department. Plot buyers are not convinced and have stopped returning calls.

news.title: WEATHER BALLOON CRASHES; OFFICIALS: 'WEATHER BALLOON'
news.message: Something with lights came down behind the water tower. Officials say it was a weather balloon, and that the four small grey bodies at the morgue are "also weather balloons." Strange people are about.
news.effect: more strange visitors and risky offers today

news.title: LAKE BLEAK MONSTER EATS A SPEEDBOAT
news.message: "It was green, it was huge and it was hungry," says the speedboat's former owner, from the shore. The parks department has closed the lake and opened a gift shop. Lake-house families are in mourning.
news.effect: more bodies to prepare, richer customers

news.title: DEAD MAN'S CURVE DOES WHAT IT SAYS ON THE SIGN
news.message: The new bypass claimed eleven motorists this week. "It's performing exactly as named," says the county engineer, who has asked for a raise. The curve mostly takes people who were too cheap for the toll road.

news.title: THE TWINS BUY A BLOWTORCH, 'FOR CRAFTS'
news.message: "We're making birdhouses," said the Twins, at exactly the same time. Three parlors have bought extra fire extinguishers. The rest have taken out extra insurance on their competitors.

news.title: COUSIN SAL OPENS WALK-IN CLINIC IN A WALK-IN FREEZER
news.message: "Cheaper than the hospital and closer to the morgue," says Sal, M.D. (University of P.O. Box 411). Patients are walking in. Undertakers are wheeling them out. The hospital has cut prices to compete.
news.effect: more bodies to prepare, hospital 20% cheaper

news.title: MAYOR UNVEILS SECOND STATUE OF MAYOR
news.message: "The first one was lonely," explains the Mayor. The new statue faces the old one across the square; both are pointing at something important. The money came out of the permit office, which is now charging more.
news.effect: City Hall permits 25% dearer, families spend 5% more (civic pride)

news.title: FENWICK PROMISES 'FEWER STATUES, MORE FLOSSING'
news.message: Mayoral hopeful Doris Fenwick, retired dentist, held a rally at the Pale Horse Cafe and handed out free coffee and toothbrushes. The Mayor replied by announcing a third statue. The town is in a pleasant mood.

news.title: MORTY THE SKELETON MADE HONORARY CITIZEN
news.message: "He has never littered, never complained and never asked for a pothole to be filled," said the Mayor, presenting the key to the city to a box of bones. Suddenly everybody wants to end up like Morty.

news.title: BLAINE OPENS DISCOUNT FUNERAL HOME
news.message: "SAME DEATH, HALF THE PRICE," reads Blaine's new billboard on Route 9, directly under the face of one of our morticians. Our families are reading it too, and they have brought calculators.

news.title: BLAINE FUNERAL HOME CLOSED: 'THEY USED BOXES'
news.message: "Cardboard boxes," confirms a Blaine health inspector. "Labeled FRAGILE." Blaine's grieving families are driving over to us in shame, and in money.

news.title: OBSERVATORY: METEOR 'PROBABLY FINE'
news.message: "It is getting bigger, but so is our telescope budget," says the county observatory. The town is getting its affairs in order, mostly by buying very nice funerals for each other in advance.

news.title: FOUR-HOUR SERMON: NINE DIE OF OLD AGE IN PEWS
news.message: "I had a lot to get off my chest," said Father Smyth. The pews were cleared by stretcher. Mourners are calmer than usual today, having done most of their grieving during the second hour.
news.effect: +1 turn today, customers a little calmer

news.title: YANG'S FORTUNE PRINTER JAMS ON 'YOU WILL DIE'
news.message: Every cookie at Yang's last night said the same thing. June says the printer is fixed and that she "doesn't see the problem, it's accurate." Superstitious families are spending big, just in case.
news.effect: families spend 5% more, customers haggle less

news.title: MAYOR LOWERS SPEED LIMIT TO 15 AFTER HEARSE PASSES HIM
news.message: "It was going so fast the deceased was waving," complained the Mayor. Processions are crawling, and so is everybody else. Families waiting at the parlor have nowhere better to be.

news.title: DI-MART CLERK BLINKS; STORE RAISES PRICES IN PANIC
news.message: Shoppers say Elijah blinked at 2:14 p.m. Tuesday, for the first time on record. Di-Mart management has raised prices "until we know what it means." Elijah has not commented, or blinked again.

news.title: OBITUARIES PRINTED ONE DAY EARLY
news.message: A printing mix-up put tomorrow's obituaries in today's paper. Eight of the people named called to complain. Four have since stopped calling. Undertakers are advised to read ahead and bring a tape measure.

news.title: FLORISTS' STRIKE: MOURNERS BRING WEEDS
news.message: "A dandelion is a flower if you love someone enough," says the florists' union, which is also charging double for dandelions. Families are irritable and holding their wallets closer.

news.title: BELLS BRING BUS TOURS TO ST. MORTIMER'S
news.message: The rebuilt steeple now rings twice for every funeral, and Father Smyth has started charging for the second ring. Out-of-town mourners are booking the full ring package and tipping the ringer, who is Father Smyth's nephew and a little deaf.
news.effect: families spend 5% more, customers a little calmer

news.title: VANE'S GARAGE CHARGES MOURNERS BY THE HOUR
news.message: Lucius Vane's garage on the old church lot has opened with a four-dollar minimum and a sign reading ALL SPACES FINAL. Funeral processions now pay by the hour. Father Smyth was seen leaving a hymn book under a windshield wiper.
news.effect: Reaper Club cover 1 tag cheaper, poorer customers

news.title: BIGTOWN CHARGES FOR PARKING AT FUNERALS; FAMILIES RETURN
news.message: Families who fled to Bigtown found the meters did not blink and the cough had followed them anyway. Several have come home to Deathville, where parlor parking is free and the cough has moved on to Blaine. They are very polite about it, and very tired.
news.effect: customers haggle less, families spend 5% more

news.title: COMMEMORATIVE COUGH DROP SPORTS {mayor}'S FACE
news.message: To mark the cure, {mayor} has issued a cough drop bearing a portrait of {mayor}. Sales are brisk, mostly among people who have since been advised not to chew it. The Mayor's office says the profits go "to the cause", and the cause is the Mayor's office.
news.effect: City Hall permits 10% dearer, families spend 5% more

news.title: UNKNOWN UNDERTAKER STATUE GROWS A SECOND HAND
news.message: Overnight someone added a second hand to the statue in the square, also palm up. Experts say pigeons cannot have done it. Mourners leave coins in both palms for luck, and the council collects them at dawn "for upkeep".

news.title: MORTY ISSUED CITY HALL STAFF BADGE, PARKING SPACE
news.message: Morty has held the City Hall door since his concession and has not missed a day. "Best employee we've had," says {mayor}. "He has never asked for a day off to bury a relative." Permit clerks, inspired, are working through lunch.

news.title: HONORARY MAYOR MORTY OPENS BUS SHELTER BY STANDING NEXT TO IT
news.message: The ribbon was cut by {mayor}, who is still allowed the scissors. Morty gave a speech, which was a nod. The town is in an unusually good mood, though the shelter has no roof and Morty has been seen sitting under it anyway.

news.title: RACCOON IN HAT SENTENCED TO COMMUNITY SERVICE AT GRAVEYARD
news.message: The county court gave the raccoon two hundred hours tending graves under the supervision of Deacon, who volunteered. Police say a human mastermind remains at large. The raccoon has already tidied Row C and is described as "very good with a trowel".

news.title: FAMILIES FILE 61 'MISSING GRANDPA' REPORTS; POLICE FILE UNDER G
news.message: Row C is still empty and the filing cabinet is full. Police say most of the grandpas will "turn up eventually, one way or another". Families are hurrying to book plots they can watch from the window, and buying very good locks.
news.effect: grave robbers +10 luck, families spend 5% more

news.title: ELIJAH PROMOTED TO ASSISTANT TO THE ASSISTANT MANAGER
news.message: Di-Mart's employee of the century now has a lanyard, a laminated schedule and a stool. He did not blink during the announcement, and the stool remains unused. The staff discount now covers "all friends of Elijah", a list that includes every undertaker in town.

news.title: DI-MART ADDS SURCHARGE TO COVER THE PAPERWORK OF THE PAPERWORK
news.message: Elijah's holding company has issued a surcharge notice for the cost of issuing surcharge notices. Caskets are up. Elijah is at the register, where the forms are stacked to the ceiling and the ceiling is stacked on Elijah.

news.title: TWINS WRITE FROM BLAINE: 'WEATHER'S NICE, NOTHING ON FIRE'
news.message: The postcard to the fire brigade is signed twice and says the Twins are "taking up pottery". The kiln has worried the Blaine fire brigade, which has asked to borrow our dalmatian. The dalmatian declined and went back to sleep on the hose.
news.effect: fewer risky offers, fewer bodies to prepare

news.title: ELM STREET REBUILDS IN 'FIRE-RESISTANT CARDBOARD'
news.message: The Twins' insurers have funded a rebuild in materials that "should hold in light weather". Contractors have hung a banner reading UNDER NEW MANAGEMENT; the previous management is in Blaine. Hammers are scarce, and so are the walls they are for.
news.effect: parlor upgrades 10% dearer, families spend 5% more

news.title: WITHERS' NEW HEARSE CIRCLES THE REAPER CLUB 'FOR PRACTICE'
news.message: Old Man Withers, winner of his own death pool, drives a lap of the club every hour on the hour. "Dress rehearsal," he says. "Somebody has to know where the brake is." Gamblers have opened a second pool on how long the first one lasts.
news.effect: Reaper Club cover 1 tag dearer, more unusual customers

news.title: WITHERS PLANS SECOND WAKE, 'BIGGER, WITH A BAND'
news.message: After the success of the first, Old Man Withers will hold a living wake every Saturday until he really does die, "so everyone's in practice". Father Smyth has ordered more dry cake. The town is in a generous mood, and so are its wallets.
news.effect: families spend 5% more, customers a little calmer

news.title: 'DIE LOCAL' BUMPER STICKERS SELL OUT
news.message: The stickers have sold out twice. A man with very white teeth was seen buying one in Bigtown and pretending it was a gift. Families say they want a parlor with "a real front desk and a real smell".
news.effect: families spend 5% more, customers haggle less

news.title: PLOT RENTS NOW TRAVEL TO BIGTOWN BY BUS
news.message: Cemetery rents leave for SolemnCorp's head office on the morning bus and come back, reduced, on the afternoon one. "The delay is for your convenience," says the man with the teeth. The grass has never looked better, and nobody can afford to stand on it.

news.title: SOLEMNCORP HOLD MUSIC REQUESTED AT TWO WEDDINGS
news.message: The Bigtown call center is still answering, and its slow organ hold music has become a minor hit. The man with the teeth was seen waiting in the queue himself. "We are very sorry," says the voice on the line. "Your call is important to the deceased."

news.title: GERTIE'S CANCELLED CRUISE SINKS AT THE DOCK
news.message: The ship Nurse Gertie was meant to board went down before leaving the harbor. Everyone got off, apart from the buffet. "I'd have been in the good lifeboat, prince," she says. Cousin Sal is selling lifeboats, which are cheaper than the hospital and about as sound.

news.title: HEAD NURSE SAL ISSUES HOSPITAL BILLS ON NAPKINS
news.message: Under Sal, bills are written on cafeteria napkins and payable "in kind or in cash, preferably in cash". Discharges keep going out the back door. Gertie is saving every napkin and says they will be "evidence, prince".
news.effect: hospital 20% cheaper, more bodies to prepare

news.title: LAKE BLEAK FERRY REOPENS AS MUSEUM, GIFT SHOP
news.message: The old ferry is moored at the shore with a ticket booth staffed by Lucius Vane. "I'm told it's authentic," he says. "I'm told that about everything." Families of the passengers are at last arranging proper services, and asking about group rates.
news.effect: more bodies to prepare, families spend 5% more

news.title: VISITORS ASKED TO STOP FEEDING LAKE MONSTER SANDWICHES
news.message: County scientists say the creature is shy, prefers carp and has been seen leaving the lake with a picnic basket. A swimmer in an inflatable duck is now described as "a smaller swimmer". The county calls this "a matter for the insurance".
news.effect: families spend 5% more, a few more bodies to prepare

news.title: {mayor} FRAMES NO-CONFIDENCE VOTE, HANGS IT BY THE STATUES
news.message: The council's four-to-one vote now hangs in City Hall between the second and third statues. "It's an honour to be doubted by so many," said {mayor}. The permit office, still nervous, is keeping its prices down.

news.title: FENWICK FILES FOR 'EVERY OFFICE WITH A BALLOT'
news.message: Doris Fenwick was turned down for the Parks Department on the grounds that it is a department. She is handing out toothbrushes outside the library, and a statue of {mayor} has been moved to make room. The town is in a pleasant mood.

news.title: {mayor} CUTS RIBBON ON FIRST HEARSE-ONLY PARKING METER
news.message: The meter takes coins and, in a pinch, condolences. {mayor} cut the ribbon with garden shears and a great deal of confidence. Funeral processions park free; everyone else parks wherever the meter is pointing.

news.title: AUDIT FINDS {mayor} KEPT ONE PROMISE, BY ACCIDENT
news.message: The Funeral Times counted forty-one campaign promises. {mayor} kept the one about more funerals. The audit was presented at a press conference, and {mayor} thanked the auditors and asked them to leave by the side door.

news.title: {mayor} BANS MONDAYS, SETTLES FOR LONGER FRIDAY
news.message: The order was withdrawn after a clerk pointed out that Mondays are load-bearing. Business owners are cautiously optimistic and have not been told which Friday. Several parlors have already booked it.

news.title: {mayor} NAMES SIXTH STATUE 'THE SECOND-BEST ONE'
news.message: With no rival on the horizon, {mayor} has unveiled another statue of {mayor} and a plinth for the next. The permit office paid for it. Residents now use the statues as landmarks, mostly to say "turn left at him".

news.title: {mayor} 'MORE OF A SUGGESTION THAN A MAYOR,' SAYS COUNCIL
news.message: Nobody else would run, so {mayor} remains in office and fills potholes with press releases. A suggestion box has been installed outside City Hall. It is currently a very large pothole, and it is full.

news.title: {mournes} SLASHES PRICES
news.message: "Why pay more to be put in less?" asks the new {mournes} billboard on Elm Street. Families are arriving with the flyer in one hand and a red pen in the other.

news.title: CORONER GONE FISHING
news.message: {coroner} is at Lake Bleak for the week. In his absence the county has authorized "anyone with a clipboard" to sign death certificates. Paperwork is quick, confident and occasionally signed by Morty.
