news.title: INSPECTOR MUDGE BUYS A NEW FLASHLIGHT
news.message: "It has three settings," says Inspector Mudge. "Bright, brighter and closed by order of the county." To give businesses no excuse, City Hall has cut permit fees for the day. Nobody feels better.

ordinances.title: Raise the Speed Limit to 85
ordinances.text: "Get where you're going faster, or don't get there at all. The Mayor's office calculates that the average funeral is now twelve minutes closer." Speeding fines will come out of family budgets.
ordinances.effect: +1 turn a day, customers spend 5% less

ordinances.title: Open Carry for Morticians
ordinances.text: "A shovel is a tool. A tool is a right. The Mayor reminds every mortician to keep their shovel holstered in church and pointed down at funerals."
ordinances.effect: fights pay 25% more, customers arrive edgier

ordinances.title: Graveyard Quiet Hours
ordinances.text: "Let the dead rest, and let the neighbours sleep. The Mayor's office has hired a man with a lantern and a very loud whistle."
ordinances.effect: no graveyard duels, grave robbers -15 luck, calmer customers

ordinances.title: Small Business Tax Holiday
ordinances.text: "The town can't afford it, so we're doing it twice as hard. Deathville Savings has kindly agreed to cover the difference out of your interest."
ordinances.effect: upgrades 10% off, permits half price, savings -0.1% a day

ordinances.title: Mandatory Embalming Act
ordinances.text: "Everybody gets the works. It's the law now. The Mayor's office would like to thank the Embalmers' Guild for writing it, and for the fruit basket."
ordinances.effect: families spend 5% more but haggle harder, more bodies to prepare

ordinances.title: Sin Tax on Nightlife
ordinances.text: "If you can afford to dance, you can afford to fill a pothole. The proceeds go to the bank, the church, and absolutely nowhere else."
ordinances.effect: Reaper Club cover +2 tags, bingo pays the whole pot, savings +0.2% a day

ordinances.title: Downtown Curfew After Dark
ordinances.text: "Nothing good happens after nine o'clock, except the Mayor's poker game, which is exempt." Hired muscle will need to make an appointment.
ordinances.effect: fights pay 25% less, hit men 50% dearer

ordinances.title: Bingo Hall Roof Levy
ordinances.text: "The church roof leaks on the faithful and the Lord has asked us to do something. The church will keep a little more of the pot. A dry church is a calm town."
ordinances.effect: the church keeps twice the bingo cut, customers a little calmer

ordinances.title: Tariff on Out-of-Town Caskets
ordinances.text: "Buy local, die local. Every Deathville casket is now made in Deathville, by Di-Mart, from parts. Proud families will spend accordingly."
ordinances.effect: Di-Mart caskets 10% dearer, families spend 5% more

ordinances.title: Cemetery Property Tax
ordinances.text: "Every plot owner pays a fair share for the roads. The dead don't use the roads, but their visitors do, and they drive like they're grieving." The money goes to the contractors.
ordinances.effect: plot income -25%, upgrades 10% off

ordinances.title: Eternal Rest Subsidy
ordinances.text: "Land is the future. Also the past, which is where we keep it." The town will top up every plot owner's rent, and Di-Mart has agreed to pay for it at the casket counter.
ordinances.effect: plot income +25%, Di-Mart caskets 5% dearer

ordinances.title: Police Overtime Act
ordinances.text: "More officers, more hours, more donuts. The Commissioner has promised to look at the graveyard at least once a night, from the car." Paid for out of your savings interest.
ordinances.effect: grave robbers -10 luck, hit men 30% dearer, savings -0.1% a day

ordinances.title: Hospital Funding Drive
ordinances.text: "A healthy town is a happy town," says the Mayor's office, which polled the undertakers and has decided to ignore them. Treatment is cheaper. People keep surviving.
ordinances.effect: hospital 40% cheaper, fewer customers (more empty waits)

ordinances.title: Usury Cap
ordinances.text: "No bank in Deathville may charge more than Cousin Sal. Deathville Savings has responded by paying savers less, out of what the teller calls spite and the bank calls policy."
ordinances.effect: loans 1% a day cheaper, savings -0.1% a day

ordinances.title: Sound Money Act
ordinances.text: "A dollar saved is a dollar the Mayor can borrow later. Savers will be rewarded. Borrowers will be looked at, over glasses, for a long time."
ordinances.effect: savings +0.2% a day, loans 1% a day dearer

ordinances.title: Graveyard Open All Night
ordinances.text: "The dead don't keep office hours, so why should their visitors? The cemetery gate will stay open around the clock." The groundskeeper will be asleep for some of the clock.
ordinances.effect: grave robbers +10 luck, customers a little edgier

ordinances.title: Sunday Closing Law
ordinances.text: "One day of rest a week for every working undertaker. Father Smyth insisted. The Mayor insisted harder, since it's the only day he can get a tee time."
ordinances.effect: -1 turn a day, customers calmer and 1 patience longer

ordinances.title: Billboard Ban on Route 9
ordinances.text: "Too many faces over the highway. Drivers are crashing into the competition." No new permits without a hearing. The contractors, now idle, will work for less.
ordinances.effect: permits 50% dearer, upgrades 10% off

ordinances.title: Honest Games Act
ordinances.text: "The Reaper Club will be inspected for fairness by an inspector of the Mayor's choosing, who will be paid in chips." The club lowers its cover. The back room raises its prices.
ordinances.effect: Reaper Club cover 1 tag cheaper, hit men 25% dearer

ordinances.title: Dry County Act
ordinances.text: "A sober town is a polite town, and a polite town pays its parking tickets." The Reaper Club will be serving punch. Something will be in the punch.
ordinances.effect: Reaper Club cover +2 tags, calmer customers, hospital 20% cheaper

ordinances.title: Zoo Tiger Enclosure Bond
ordinances.text: "A bigger cage for the tiger, and a gift shop. Hank Pruitt says it's for public safety. The tiger says nothing, which is new." Taxes go up to pay for it.
ordinances.effect: more unusual customers, poorer customers

ordinances.title: Funeral Price Transparency Act
ordinances.text: "Every price on the wall, in big letters, next to Blaine's price, in small letters." Families will haggle and spend less, but the town will respect an honest sale.
ordinances.effect: customers haggle harder and spend 5% less, sales earn 10% more BP

ordinances.title: Bereavement Leave Act
ordinances.text: "Every grieving family gets three days off work to choose a casket properly." Unpaid. Families will take their time, and take less money with them.
ordinances.effect: customers 1 patience longer, spend 5% less

ordinances.title: Hearse-Only Fast Lane
ordinances.text: "The dead have waited long enough. A lane for hearses only, from the hospital to the cemetery, with a toll booth." The toll will be collected at City Hall and at Di-Mart.
ordinances.effect: +1 turn a day, permits 25% dearer, Di-Mart caskets 5% dearer

ordinances.title: Extended Happy Hour
ordinances.text: "Happiness is good for business, and so are two-for-one shots." Lucius Vane has donated to the campaign. Mourners may arrive a little tipsy and a little loud.
ordinances.effect: Reaper Club cover 1 tag cheaper, customers arrive crankier

ordinances.title: Neighborhood Watch Grants
ordinances.text: "Eyes on every street, paid for by the town." The Twins have volunteered to captain it. Fights and graverobbing are down. Some other things are up.
ordinances.effect: fights pay 20% less, grave robbers -10 luck, more risky offers

signage.name: Signage Permit (Form 9-B)
signage.description: Authorises one (1) likeness of the applicant above Route 9. The words YOU'RE NEXT are not on the list of prohibited phrases. We checked.

zoning.name: Zoning Variance
zoning.description: Reclassifies the lot behind your parlor from Former Landfill to Garden. Any humming from the soil after dark is the property owner's concern.

crematory.name: Crematory Emissions Permit
crematory.description: Certifies your smoke as mostly wood. Complaints from Blaine are filed in the round cabinet under the desk.

bank.savingsIntro: `$Prudence the teller looks at you over her glasses. You have `w${savings}`$ in savings, earning `w{rate}%`$ a day (on up to `w${cap}`$). Cash on hand: `w${cash}`$. Money in the bank can't be stolen from your till, she points out, slowly.
bank.depositPrompt: How much do you want to deposit?
bank.withdrawPrompt: How much do you want to withdraw?
bank.deposited: `$Prudence counts your `w${money}`$ twice, licks her thumb, counts it a third time and stamps the book.
bank.withdrew: `$Prudence hands over `w${money}`$ one bill at a time, as if saying goodbye to each of them.
bank.badAmount: `$Prudence stares at you over her glasses until you go away and come back with a real number.
bank.loanIntro: `$The bank will lend against your plots: up to `w${limit}`$ today, at `w{rate}%`$ interest a day (and `w{fee}%`$ up front, the first day's, which Prudence calls a handling fee), due in `w{days}`$ days. If you don't pay, they take your cash, your savings and your caskets, and Prudence tells the whole town. She enjoys that part.
bank.loanOwed: `$You owe the bank `w${owed}`$, due at the end of day `w{due}`$. Prudence has circled it on her calendar, in red.
bank.borrowPrompt: How much do you want to borrow?
bank.borrowed: `$The loan officer counts out `w${money}`$. "Due day {due}. We know where you bury people."
bank.repaid: `$You pay the bank `w${money}`$. Prudence almost smiles. It passes.
bank.loanClosed: The bank stops lending this close to the end of the season
bank.deadbeat: The bank doesn't lend to deadbeats
bank.loanCollected: `$Your loan came due. The bank collected `w${money}`$ from your accounts, with a note: THANK YOU FOR NOT MAKING THIS DIFFICULT.
bank.loanDefault: `4Your loan came due and you couldn't cover it. The bank took everything it could and wrote off `w${left}`4. Your name is taped in the bank window under the word NO. `5(-{bp} BP)`4`$
bank.transferIntro: `$You can send casket tags to another parlor. Prudence keeps `w{fee}%`$ (rounded up) of each transfer, for her trouble. You've sent `w{sent}`$ of `w{max}`$ wood-tag equivalents today; nobody can receive more than that a day either.
bank.transferPick: Who do you want to send tags to?
bank.transferTier: `$Which tags do you want to send to `w{name}`$?
bank.transferred: `$`w{count}`$ {tier} tag(s) are on their way to `w{name}`$. Prudence keeps `w{fee}`$ and files them under Mine.
bank.transferMail: `w{name}`$ sent you `w{count}`$ {tier} tag(s) through the bank. There is no note. There is never a note.
bank.transferTooNew: New parlors can't send tags for a few days
bank.transferLimit: That's over the daily limit ({left} more)
bank.transferTheirLimit: They can't receive any more today
bank.transferSelf: You can't send tags to yourself
bank.transferNotEnough: Not enough tags for that (and the fee)

chains.title: Parlor Chains
chains.intro: `$A chain is up to `w{max}`$ parlors sharing a season score board, like a bowling league with embalming. Founding one costs `w${fee}`$, joining one `w${join}`$, and every member pays `w${dues}`$ a day in dues. Members get a better rating, cheaper caskets, and families that walk out are sent to a chain-mate. Chain-mates can never fight, rob, burn or put a hit on each other.
chains.none: `$No chains are registered yet. The clerk has a stack of blank forms and an unearned sense of anticipation.
chains.namePrompt: What will your chain be called?
chains.invitePrompt: Which parlor do you want to invite?
chains.founded: `$The clerk registers `w{name}`$ and charges you for the ink, the pen and his time.
chains.invited: `$An invitation goes out to `w{name}`$ on City Hall letterhead, which smells of floor wax.
chains.inviteMail: `w{name}`$ invites you to join the parlor chain `w{chain}`$. Visit City Hall to accept, or to pretend you never got this.
chains.joined: `$You're now part of `w{name}`$. Somebody gives you a lapel pin and a firm, damp handshake.
chains.joinedMail: `w{name}`$ joined your chain. Make them feel welcome, or at least not robbed.
chains.left: `$You hand back the lapel pin. The clerk files your resignation under Traitors.
chains.cooldown: You left a chain recently ({days} more days)
chains.badName: `$The clerk won't register that name. Try another, preferably one the Mayor can say in church.
chains.duesUnpaid: `4You couldn't pay the ${dues} chain dues, so the chain dropped you. They want the lapel pin back by mail.`$
chains.noFriendlyFire: `${name} is in your chain. You can't do that to family.

challenge.title: Daily Challenge
challenge.intro: `$Daily Challenge `w{id}`$. Every parlor in the world gets this same day: the same families, in the same order, with the same bad attitudes. You have `w{turns}`$ turns. Make them count, and make them pay.
challenge.finished: `$The day is done. You earned `5{score} BP`$ from `w{sales}`$ sales and finished `w${money}`$ up. Your score is on the board, where everyone can judge it.

church.title: St. Mortimer's Church
church.note: Father Smyth greets you warmly, a little too warmly. You wonder if he has anything on under that robe.
greeting: `wFather Smyth: `y"Why hello there, {player}. Isn't it a wonderfully fantastic day today? Praise the Lord."
`wFather Smyth: `y"{player}! The Lord loves a cheerful giver, and so do I. Mostly the giving part."
`wFather Smyth: `y"Ah, {player}. You look like a person with something on their conscience. Or their shoe."
`wFather Smyth: `y"{player}, my child! Mind the bucket. The roof is having one of its days."
`wFather Smyth: `y"Welcome, {player}. Have a lemon bar. They're from a fresh batch. A fresher batch. A batch."
`wFather Smyth: `y"{player}! I prayed for you this morning. Not by name, but you'll know which bit."
`wFather Smyth: `y"Come in, {player}. Old Man Withers is in the back pew, so speak up. Or don't."
`wFather Smyth: `y"The prodigal undertaker returns! {player}, the collection plate has missed you terribly."
`wFather Smyth: `y"{player}. Sit anywhere except the third pew. Something happened in the third pew."
church.bingoIntro:
`$"Get your cards, ladies and gentlemen," calls Father Smyth, spinning the cage. "B-4 it's too late!"

`$There are `w{cards}`$ cards tonight; `w{sold}`$ are sold. One card wins at midnight, and its owner takes the pot: `w{pot} wood tags`$ (`w{carry}`$ carried over from nights nobody held the winner). The church keeps a small cut for the roof.

Each card costs a wood tag. Your cards: `w{mine}`$ (at most {max}). You have `w{wood}`$ wood tags.
church.bingoBought: `$Father Smyth hands you {count} card(s): number `w{numbers}`$. "Good luck, my child. Luck is a sin, but good luck."
church.bingoWinMail: `$BINGO! Your card `w#{card}`$ won last night. Father Smyth hands over `w{pot} wood tags`$ through a smile and gritted teeth.
church.bingoNews:
`7BINGO NIGHT
`^{name} won {pot} wood tags at St. Mortimer's with card #{card}. Old Man Withers says it was rigged. It wasn't. He says that every week.
church.bingoCarryNews:
`7BINGO NIGHT
`^Father Smyth called card #{card}, but nobody had bought it. The pot of {pot} wood tags rolls over to tonight. Withers is already in line.
confessed: `$You confess. Father Smyth listens, winces, and accepts `w${price}`$ "for the candles." You feel cleaner. `5(+1 karma)`$
`$Father Smyth hears you out, gasps twice, and takes `w${price}`$. "Say three Hail Marys and never tell me that again." `5(+1 karma)`$
`$A long silence through the grille, then the sound of Father Smyth writing something down. `w${price}`$ "for the candles." `5(+1 karma)`$
`$Father Smyth asks you to start again, slower, so he gets it right. `w${price}`$, and your soul is a little lighter. `5(+1 karma)`$
`$"Is that all?" asks Father Smyth. You tell him the rest. "Ah." He takes `w${price}`$ and opens a window. `5(+1 karma)`$
`$You confess to Father Smyth and, by mistake, to Old Man Withers, asleep on the other side of the booth. `w${price}`$. `5(+1 karma)`$
`$The Lord forgives everything, Father Smyth explains, and the church forgives everything over `w${price}`$. You pay. `5(+1 karma)`$
`$You tell Father Smyth about the toe tags. He laughs until he cries, then charges you `w${price}`$ for the laugh. `5(+1 karma)`$
`$"Go in peace," says Father Smyth, pocketing `w${price}`$. "Quite a lot of peace, actually. You paid for the large." `5(+1 karma)`$
church.confessCapped: `$Father Smyth closes the little window. "That's as clean as money gets you, my child. The rest you'll have to earn."
church.holyWaterBought: `$Father Smyth fills a bottle from the font and corks it with his thumb. "Bless a grieving family with it. Not your fries." You have `w{have}`$ bottle(s).
church.served: `$You lead the Sunday service. Nobody falls asleep, which is a first, and the hymn ends at the same time for everyone. `5(+{bp} BP, +{reviews} reputation)`$
tithed: `$You drop `w${money}`$ in the plate. It makes a satisfying thud. The parish newsletter will mention you. `5(+{bp} BP)`$
`$Father Smyth takes your `w${money}`$ and looks at you like a son. A son with money. `5(+{bp} BP)`$
`$You fold `w${money}`$ into the plate. Father Smyth unfolds it before it reaches the end of the pew. `5(+{bp} BP)`$
`$`w${money}`$ for the roof fund. A drop of rain lands on your head, which Father Smyth calls a sign. `5(+{bp} BP)`$
`$You tithe `w${money}`$. The organist plays a little louder for you, then stops, because you've left. `5(+{bp} BP)`$
`$Your `w${money}`$ goes in the poor box. Father Smyth explains, gently, that he is the poor. `5(+{bp} BP)`$
`$You give `w${money}`$. Old Man Withers sees you and gives a button. Father Smyth thanks you both the same. `5(+{bp} BP)`$
`$`w${money}`$ to St. Mortimer's. Your name goes on the donor board in letters Father Smyth calls generous. `5(+{bp} BP)`$

cityHall.title: City Hall
cityHall.note: City Hall smells of floor wax and broken promises. A clerk is asleep behind a sign that says ALL DEPARTMENTS.
cityHall.greeting: `w{mayor}: `y"{player}! A taxpayer, in my building! Ask not what your town can do for you. Ask what you can do for the statue fund."
cityHall.permitsIntro: `$The clerk wakes up just long enough to slide a form across the desk. It is in triplicate; the third copy is for his lunch. Some of the contractor's bigger jobs need a permit first.
cityHall.permitBought: `$The clerk stamps your `w{name}`$ eleven times, initials it twice and goes back to sleep on it.
cityHall.inspectionIntro: `$Inspector Mudge calls on one parlor in town each night, and he finds something every time unless your rating and your karma are good, or he's been looked after. A failed inspection costs a fine and your reputation.
cityHall.certifiedUntil: `$You're certified clean through day `w{until}`$. Inspector Mudge will wave at your door and keep walking.
cityHall.certified: `$Inspector Mudge walks through your parlor in four minutes, sniffs twice and signs. Clean for `w{days}`$ days, and a nice write-up in the paper.
cityHall.bribed: `$Inspector Mudge counts the envelope without looking at it. "I'm sure everything is up to code. I'm sure of it right now." `5(-2 karma)`$
cityHall.inspectPassMail: `$Inspector Mudge came by last night, ran a finger along your counter, looked at the finger for a long time and left without writing anything down.
cityHall.inspectFailMail: `4Inspector Mudge came by last night. He found a finger in the coffee maker, and it wasn't his. You were fined `w${fine}`4.`$
cityHall.inspectFailNews:
`7HEALTH CODE VIOLATION
`^Inspectors found unspeakable things at {parlor}. {name} says the finger was there when they bought the place.
cityHall.ordinanceIntro:
{current}
`$This week's ballot closes at the end of day `w{closes}`$. One vote each; the Mayor's counts double; lobbying buys more. The Mayor's office has kindly written a short, fair summary of each measure.
cityHall.noOrdinance: `$No ordinance is in force. The town runs on habit, spite and the honour system.
cityHall.noBallot: `$There's no ballot open right now. The clerk says come back on the first day of next week, and bring a pen. His is chewed.
cityHall.voted: `$You vote for `w{title}`$. The clerk puts your ballot in a box marked BALLOTS AND LUNCH.
cityHall.lobbied: `$You take a councilman to lunch on behalf of `w{title}`$. He orders the lobster, and a second lobster for later.
cityHall.ordinanceNews:
`7NEW ORDINANCE: {title}
`^{text} Passed with {votes} votes. In force all week: {effect}.
cityHall.noVotesNews:
`7COUNCIL DEADLOCKED
`^Nobody voted on this week's ordinances. The council took the week off to recover from not being asked.
cityHall.electionFiling:
`$The season's mayoral race is open for candidates until the end of day `w{until}`$. Filing costs `w${fee}`$. The Mayor gets a better parlor rating (+{rating}) from all the ribbon cuttings and a double vote on ordinances. The chauffeur is not included. Statues are optional.

Candidates so far: `w{candidates}`$.
cityHall.electionVoting:
`$Voting is open until the end of day `w{until}`$. One vote each; candidates can buy ads. The ballot box has been checked for a false bottom, by the Mayor.

Candidates: `w{candidates}`$.
cityHall.electionDone: `$The town's mayor this season is `w{name}`$. The portrait in the lobby is already crooked.
cityHall.filed: `$You're on the ballot. A photographer takes your picture for the posters. You blink. He says it's fine. It isn't.
cityHall.electionVoted: `$You vote for `w{name}`$. Democracy happens, briefly, behind a curtain.
cityHall.adsBought: `$Your face appears on every bus bench in town. Several pigeons are offended and say so.
cityHall.electedNews:
`7NEW MAYOR ELECTED
`^{name} wins the mayor's race with {votes} votes and promises to keep the town's dead in an orderly fashion, and the living in roughly the same.
cityHall.electedMail: `$You won the election! The ribbon cuttings will do your rating good and your vote on ordinances counts double. The statue fund is yours now. Spend it wisely, or on a statue.
cityHall.noElectionNews:
`7ELECTION CANCELLED
`^Nobody ran for mayor. Mayor Hollis Grubb stays on, and has commissioned a statue to mark the occasion.
cityHall.mayorMorning: `$Your mayoral chauffeur whisks you all over town, running two red lights in your honour. `w+{turns}`$ turn.

club.title: The Reaper Club
club.note: You shiver as you approach the Reaper, a rave club frequented by the underbelly of society (mostly funeral directors).
club.door: `$The bouncer, a man with a neck like a tree stump, holds out a hand. You count six fingers. "Cover's `w{cover} wooden tags`$." Behind him {owner} waves from the VIP booth.
club.necroFree: `$The bouncer sees the grave dirt under your nails, nods with respect and waves you straight through.
inside: `$You can barely hear yourself think. Somebody is dancing with a skeleton, and the skeleton is leading.
`$The DJ is playing organ music with a dance beat. Three morticians are doing the conga around a casket.
`$The bartender pours you something green. It's either absinthe or embalming fluid. Here, there's no difference.
`$A fog machine hisses in the corner. Through the fog you make out three morticians, a priest and Cousin Sal sharing a hookah.
`$The dance floor is an old embalming table lit from underneath. Nobody asks where they got it. You know where they got it.
`$Lucius Vane holds court in the VIP booth, which is a hearse with the back taken off. He raises a glass of something red at you.
`$Somebody spiked the punch bowl with formaldehyde. The punch is now technically preserved, and so is the guy face down in it.
`$A mortician in a cape screams "ASHES TO ASHES" into the microphone. The whole room screams back "DUST TO DUST."
`$The Twins are at the bar, drinking one drink through two straws, staring at you without blinking.
club.gamesIntro:
`$The house games, as honest as anything else in this town, so hold on to your wallet. You've staked `w${staked}`$ tonight; the house stops you at `w${max}`$. Over a night the house always comes out ahead. That's what makes it the house.
`wDead Man's Draw`$: you and the Reaper each draw a card; high card wins even money, a tie and the Reaper keeps half.
`wThe One-Armed Undertaker`$: three skulls pay 500 to one, three coffins 100, three bones 30, three roses 12, three worms 4; a skull on the first reel gets your stake back.
club.drawWin: `$You draw the `w{you}`$, the Reaper draws the `w{dealer}`$. You win `w${won}`$! The Reaper shuffles slowly, like he'll remember this.
club.drawLose: `$You draw the `w{you}`$, the Reaper draws the `w{dealer}`$. A bony hand rakes in your `w${won}`$. You can hear him smiling.
club.drawTie: `$You both draw the `w{you}`$. The Reaper keeps `w${won}`$ for his trouble. He calls it a handling fee.
club.slotsWin: `$It coughs up `w${won}`$! A small crowd gathers to watch you count it, then to ask for a loan.
club.slotsLose: `$Nothing. The machine burps, and the skull on the front laughs at you.
club.shotsIntro: `wFormaldehyde Roulette`$: six shot glasses, and one of them isn't vodka. Drink one and live, and the house pays a little under a fifth of your stake. Pick wrong and you lose it, and your liver files a complaint.
club.shotsWin: `$You slam it back. Vodka! The crowd cheers and the house pays `w${won}`$. Your hands are shaking. That's normal.
club.shotsLose: `4That was not vodka. You lose your stake, a good deal of your dignity and one eyebrow.`$
club.marketIntro: `$A man in a trench coat opens it. The inside is lined with merchandise. "Today's specials. Cash only. No receipts, no faces, no refunds."
club.marketBought: `$You buy `w{name}`$. When you look up, the man in the trench coat is gone, and so is your pen.
club.hitPrompt: Whose knees need a talking-to? (from ${price}, more for bigger parlors)
club.hitBooked: `$Lucius Vane takes the envelope and doesn't count it, which is worse. "Tonight. {name} won't know what hit them. Well. They'll know it was a tire iron." `5(-5 karma)`$
club.hitSelf: `$Vane looks at you for a long time. "Get help, pal. Real help. Not the kind I sell."
club.hitPeaceful: `${name} took the Peace Pledge. Even Vane has rules, and that's one of the two.
club.hitTaken: `$Somebody already paid for {name} tonight. Vane doesn't double-book. It's bad for the knees.
club.hitChain: `${name} is in your chain. Vane doesn't do family. He has a mother.
club.hitNews:
`7MORTICIAN ROUGHED UP
`^{name} was found in a dumpster behind Bill's Big Burger last night, alive, with a very clear memory of a tire iron. Police have no leads and no interest.
club.hitMail: `4Two men visited you last night and had a frank talk with you, using a tire iron for emphasis. You lose `5{bp} BP`4.`$
club.hitFoiledMail: `$Two men with a tire iron came to your parlor last night, took one look and left. You'll never know why. Maybe it was the dog.
club.hitFoiledHirer: `$Vane sends word: the job on `w{name}`$ didn't come off. No refunds. He sends a mint, though.
club.hitSnitchMail: `$The thug who came for you last night was picked up by the police and sang like a choir. `w{name}`$ paid him.
club.hitSnitchNews:
`7HIT MAN SINGS
`^A hired thug arrested outside {target}'s parlor told police that {name} paid for the job, then asked for a lawyer and a sandwich. {name} has been fined, and Father Smyth has been told.
club.hitRumour: `$Word at the Reaper Club is that somebody paid for your knees tonight. You might want a bodyguard, or a vest, or a long weekend in Blaine.
club.bodyguardBought: `$A man the size of a hearse will sleep on your porch tonight. He brought his own blanket and a teddy bear named Knuckles.
club.seanceWin: `$The candles gutter and the curtains stir. The dead whisper two names and two addresses, and that both will be needing you soon. `5(+2 customer leads)`$
club.seanceFail: `4The dead have nothing to say to you, and one of them is rude about it, at length. `5(-3 luck)`4`$

graveyard.title: Town Graveyard
graveyard.note: A dense fog covers the many mounds and headstones that make up the town graveyard. You see other morticians dancing through the memorials as they clean, adjust and make room for new occupants.
graveyard.intro:
`$Nothing relaxes you like a visit to the town grave site.

Your parlor has `w{plots}`$ plots out here. Your row is marked by `w{monument}`$.
`$You have time for `w{duels}`$ more duel today.
graveyard.noMonument: a wooden stake with your name on it in crayon
graveyard.monumentsIntro: `wNed the stonecutter lights a cigarette off a memorial candle: `$"Your row's got {current}. People judge a parlor by its dead. Bigger stone, bigger reputation. Bigger invoice, too."
graveyard.monumentLine: `$Next up: `w{name}`$ for `w${price}`$. The town will talk about it for days (`5+{bp} BP`$, and a better rating while it stands).
graveyard.monumentBought: `$Ned unveils `w{name}`$ with a flourish and a cough. A small crowd gathers to look at it, then at you. `5(+{bp} BP)`$
graveyard.allBuilt: `$You already own the biggest thing in the graveyard. Ned suggests a moat. You say you'll think about it.
tended: `$You pull weeds, straighten flowers and apologize to a few headstones. You feel lucky. `5(+{luck} luck)`$
`$You rake the paths and wipe the bird mess off old Mrs. Hubble. Mourners nod at you. `5(+{luck} luck)`$
`$You swap the plastic flowers on a forgotten grave for slightly better plastic flowers. `5(+{luck} luck)`$
`$You straighten a leaning headstone. It leans back the moment you turn around, but the thought counts. `5(+{luck} luck)`$
`$You scrub the moss off a row of old soldiers. One was a general. Now he looks like one again. `5(+{luck} luck)`$
`$Deacon the graveyard dog follows you down the row and doesn't bite you once. That has to be a sign. `5(+{luck} luck)`$
`$You fill in a hole somebody left open overnight, and decide not to wonder what came out of it. `5(+{luck} luck)`$
`$You polish the plaque on a grave nobody visits. A cold hand touches your shoulder, but in a nice way. `5(+{luck} luck)`$
`$You read every name in Row B out loud. A widow sees you and decides you are either a saint or a weirdo. `5(+{luck} luck)`$
graveyard.tendedLead: `$A widow watering a grave asks for your card. Her husband "isn't looking well, and he's started making that noise." `5(a customer lead)`$
graveyard.tendedAssociate: `$Father Smyth sees you at work and mentions you in Sunday's sermon, favourably for once. `5(extra reputation)`$
robFound: `$You dig up a fresh one and relieve the deceased of `w${money}`$ in jewelry. He won't miss it. He won't miss anything.
`$Gold fillings, a pocket watch and a ring come to `w${money}`$. You fill the hole back in. Mostly.
`$She was buried with her purse. Inside: `w${money}`$, a lipstick and a note that says I KNEW IT. You leave the note.
`$Cufflinks and a tie pin, `w${money}`$ at the pawn shop. The tie itself is hideous. You let him keep it.
`$A fresh plot and a fat wallet: `w${money}`$. His family meant it for the ferryman. You tip yourself instead.
`$You pry `w${money}`$ worth of gold off a set of teeth. They are not his teeth. You don't ask whose.
`$A velvet pouch tucked by the pillow holds `w${money}`$ in old coins. He didn't trust banks either.
`$A wedding ring and a medal for bravery fetch `w${money}`$. The medal makes you feel bad for nearly a block.
graveyard.robSilver: `$You find a silver casket tag still wired to the handle. Nobody tags a casket this nice for nothing. `w+1 silver tag`$.
graveyard.robCaught: `4The groundskeeper catches you elbow-deep in Mr. Abernathy. Deacon catches the rest of you. You pay a `w${fine}`4 fine and the whole town hears about it.`$
look: `$Two morticians argue over who gets the plot by the oak tree. The oak tree has seen this before.
`$A fresh grave has been dug and filled three times today. Somebody can't make up their mind.
`$A raven lands on a headstone, looks at you, and leaves without a word. Rude.
`$Old Man Withers is walking the rows with a tape measure, pricing the good spots. He waves the tape at you.
`$Somebody has left flowers on the Mayor's family plot. The Mayor's family is still alive. The card says SOON.
`$Ned the stonecutter is carving a headstone with a date that hasn't happened yet. He covers it when you look.
`$Deacon is digging with great enthusiasm in Row D. The groundskeeper calls him off, then calls the police.
`$A mourner in black is weeping at a grave. You walk closer. It's one of your rivals, practising.
`$The Twins are on a bench eating sandwiches. They stop chewing when you pass, at exactly the same time.
`$Father Smyth is blessing graves at a brisk walk, one every three seconds, like a man feeding parking meters.
graveyard.lookRows: `$The biggest rows of headstones belong to: `w{list}`$.

duel.prompt: Who do you want to meet among the headstones?
duel.youFirst: `$You meet `w{name}`$ between the rows. You have more dead out here than they do, so you know the ground. You strike first.
duel.theyFirst: `$You meet `w{name}`$ between the rows. They know this ground better than you do, and they swing before you've finished your speech.
duel.youHit: `$You whack `w{name}`$ with a chunk of headstone for `4{damage}`$ damage. The name on it was spelled wrong anyway.
duel.youMiss: `$You swing at `w{name}`$ and hit a marble cherub instead. It does not flinch. It never flinches.
duel.theyHit: `w{name}`$ cracks you across the back with a shovel for `4{damage}`$ damage.
duel.theyMiss: `w{name}`$ swings, misses, and kicks over a vase of lilies. A nearby widow gasps.
duel.shoveIn: `$You shove `w{name}`$ into an open grave! `4{damage}`$ damage. You swing while they climb out, and they lose their next move doing it.
duel.shoveFail: `$You lunge to shove `w{name}`$, miss, and land face first on a footstone. They take advantage.
duel.theyShove: `w{name}`$ shoves you into an open grave! `4{damage}`$ damage. They swing, then get a free swing while you claw your way out, and you lose your next move.
duel.theyShoveFail: `w{name}`$ tries to shove you into a grave and trips over a wreath. Free swing for you.
duel.won: `$`w{name}`$ goes down among the dead and stays there a while. You win `5{bp} BP`$ and polite applause from a funeral nearby.
duel.lost: `4You wake up face down on somebody's grave. `w{name}`4 wins. You lose `5{bp} BP`4.`$
duel.yielded: `$You throw down your shovel. `w{name}`$ accepts your surrender with a smirk. You lose `5{bp} BP`$, but nothing is broken.
duel.wonMail: `w{name}`$ challenged you in the graveyard and lost, badly, in front of a funeral. You win `5{bp} BP`$.
duel.lostMail: `w{name}`$ beat you senseless in the graveyard. The mourners at the next plot got their money's worth. You lose `5{bp} BP`$.
duel.yieldMail: `w{name}`$ challenged you in the graveyard, then lost their nerve and threw down their shovel. `5+{bp} BP`$.
duel.crime:
`7GRAVEYARD BRAWL
`^{winner} beat {loser} among the headstones last night. Several of the dead were disturbed, and one has filed a complaint.
duel.selfPeaceful: You took the Peace Pledge. No duels for you
duel.targetPeaceful: `${name} took the Peace Pledge. The groundskeeper won't allow it.
duel.chainMate: `${name} is in your chain. Brawling with family is bad for business.
duel.rivalTired: `${name} has been beaten in the graveyard enough for one day.
duel.sheltered: `${name}'s chain has taken enough beatings today. Their friends are watching the gate.
duel.self: `$You can't duel yourself. You've tried. It was in the paper.
duel.nobody: `$There's nobody here to fight but the dead, and they always win eventually.

hints.karmaTooHigh: Your conscience is too clean for this

hospital.title: Hospital
hospital.note: The hospital smells of bleach and boiled carrots. The Nurse looks up from a crossword about bones, which she is winning.
hospital.greeting: `w{nurse}: `y"Back again, {player}? What did you break this time, prince? Don't tell me. Show me. No, tell me."
hospital.injuryLine: `$`w{name}`$: heals in `w{days}`$ day(s), or `w${price}`$ to fix today.
hospital.noInjuries: `$You're in one piece, more or less. Injuries from fights would show up here, and on your face.
hospital.treated: `$The doctor fixes your `w{name}`$ and charges you for the tongue depressor, the lollipop and the look he gave you.
hospital.leadIntro: `$The Nurse knows who's in intensive care and who won't be leaving it. For `w${price}`$ she'll put your card in the right hand. `5({karma} karma, a sure and richer customer)`$
leadBought: `$The Nurse tucks the money in her shoe. "Room 212. Ask for the daughter."
`$"Bed six. Pancreas. Give it till Thursday." She winks. You wish she hadn't.
`$She slides a menu across the desk with a name circled on the back. "He had the chowder, prince. Nobody survives the chowder."
`$"Third floor, the room with the balloons. The balloons are optimistic." The money disappears into her cardigan.
`$"Mrs. Teague in 14 wants a pink casket and won't shut up about it. Bring a brochure." She pats your cheek.
`$"There's a man in the cardiac ward who just read his bill." She crosses herself and counts your money.
`$"Wait till the priest comes out. Then go in looking sad, not hungry." She has clearly done this before.
`$She writes a room number on your hand in pen. "And wash that off before the family sees it, prince."
`$"The family in the waiting room has been fighting about the will for an hour. They'll want it fast and fancy."
hospital.leadMax: You already have plenty of leads
hospital.armorSaved: `$Your vest takes the worst of it. The vest is ruined. You are only bruised, and slightly embarrassed.
hospital.leadArrives: `$The family your lead promised walks in, wallet first, right on time. The Nurse is never wrong.

world.quietNews: Nothing in the paper worth dying for.

weather.label: Clear
morning: A clear, crisp morning. Perfect weather for a funeral, or for causing one.
The sun is out. Somewhere a bird is singing. You find this suspicious.
Not a cloud in the sky. The mourners will have to supply their own gloom.
Blue skies over Deathville. The undertakers squint at it like it owes them money.
A beautiful day. Old Man Withers is out on his porch, outliving people at a steady pace.
Sunshine. The headstones gleam. The groundskeeper polishes the ones that pay.
A perfect morning. Even Morty looks a little less dead in this light.
Clear skies and a light breeze. The kind of day people say they want to be buried on.

weather.label: Overcast
morning: A low grey sky, like the lid of a cheap casket. The town is subdued.
Overcast. Nobody is happy, but nobody is angry either. Ideal.
The clouds sit on the town like a wet blanket. Families arrive quiet and resigned.
Grey all morning. Father Smyth says it's the Lord's way of setting the mood.
A sky the colour of embalming fluid. You feel strangely at home.
Flat grey light. Everyone looks a little like a photograph of themselves.
Overcast and still. Even the crows are speaking softly.
A dull, sleepy morning. Customers will sit where you put them.

weather.label: Rain
morning: It's pouring. Rain makes people sad, and sad people buy flowers.
A grey drizzle. The mourners will cry harder and haggle less.
Rain on the windows. Families come in damp and too miserable to argue.
A steady rain. The graves will need topping up again.
It's raining on every funeral in town. Business is good and soggy.
Rain all day. Someone's umbrella is already in your umbrella stand. Now it's yours.
Wet and cold. The tissues are on special and you put them by the door.
Rain hammers the hearse roof. Customers want to get the paperwork done and go home.

weather.label: Fog
morning: A dense fog covers the mounds and headstones. A good night to dig where you shouldn't.
Fog so thick you can't see your own hearse. The groundskeeper can't see you either.
The fog rolls in off Lake Bleak. Something in it is humming.
Pea soup out there. Shady men in long coats are suddenly very easy to talk to.
Fog. You hear a shovel somewhere in the graveyard, and then another one answering it.
Thick fog all morning. Deacon the graveyard dog is barking at nothing in particular.
The fog hides everything, which is how the Reaper Club likes it.
You can't see the end of the street. Somebody down there is selling something.
weather.effect: +15 luck robbing graves, more risky offers

weather.label: Thunderstorm
morning: Thunder. Every customer jumps at each crack and wants to get this over with.
Lightning hit the church again. Father Smyth is taking it personally.
A storm rolls over town. The power flickers and the cooler groans.
Thunder rattles the display caskets. One of them rattles back.
Lightning, then thunder, then a scream from the bingo hall. Business as usual.
The storm knocked over a tree onto the Mayor's first statue. The second statue saw it all.
Rain sideways and thunder overhead. Customers are short-tempered and soaking.
A wild storm. Somebody's toupee went past your window at forty miles an hour.

weather.label: Scorcher
morning: It's a hundred and four in the shade, and the shade is in the cooler with the bodies.
A blistering morning. The asphalt is soft and the tempers are short.
Heat haze over the graveyard. The flowers wilted before the funeral started.
The thermometer outside Di-Mart gave up and fell off the wall.
So hot the ice in your lemonade evaporated on the way to your mouth.
A scorcher. The fans are on full and the families are sweating through their black.
Heat like an oven. Your Incinerator feels left out.
Hot enough to fry an egg on the hearse. Somebody is trying, outside.

weather.label: Muggy
morning: Damp and sticky. The bodies won't keep like they ought to.
Humid as a swamp. Every corpse in town needs attention by noon.
The air is soup. Your embalming room smells like a decision you'll regret.
Muggy and close. Flies are lining up outside the cooler.
Sticky weather. The deceased are getting ahead of themselves.
Wet heat. The formaldehyde is sweating more than you are.
It's muggy enough that the graveyard is steaming. Nobody wants to know why.
Thick, warm air. A good day to have a strong stomach and a full storeroom of fluid.

weather.label: Snow
morning: Snow. The ground is too hard to dig, so families are paying extra for the crypt.
Fresh snow over the headstones. The graveyard looks almost respectable.
A white morning. The hearse slides into the lot sideways, which is now its parking style.
Snow falling soft and slow. Families feel sentimental and generous.
Snowed in. Somebody built a snowman with a shovel and a toe tag.
A heavy snowfall. The digging crew charges double and drinks triple.
Snow on everything. It's hard to haggle when your teeth are chattering.
Snow. The kind of day that makes people want a warm, expensive casket.

weather.label: Cold Snap
morning: Bitter cold. The bodies keep themselves today. Your embalming table gets a rest.
A cold snap. The cooler is the warmest room in the parlor.
Frost on the inside of the windows. The deceased are well preserved by nature.
Freezing. Morty's joints creak in sympathy.
So cold the groundskeeper's dog is wearing the groundskeeper's coat.
Below zero. Nobody's going off in a hurry, not even the dead.
An icy morning. The flowers out front are frozen in a very nice arrangement.
Cold enough to keep a body on the porch. Three of your neighbours are doing it.

weather.label: Hail
morning: Hail the size of golf balls. Di-Mart's casket delivery is covered in dents.
Hailstorm. Elijah is selling dented caskets at a small discount and a straight face.
Hail bounces off the hearse. It now has a texture, like a golf ball.
Ice from the sky all morning. The Mayor's statues are both pockmarked.
A short, violent hailstorm. Several umbrellas are dead. You offer a group rate.
Hail on the roof like a drum solo. The storeroom has some new dents.
Hailstones in the gutters. Di-Mart's loading dock looks like a battlefield.
Hail, then sun, then hail. Di-Mart is calling the dents 'character'.

weather.label: Gale
morning: High winds. Things blow in through the door that aren't customers.
A gale off the lake. Your sign is now in Blaine.
Wind howling through the graveyard. The wreaths are migrating south.
A gusty day. Every few minutes something bangs against the parlor and you go look.
The wind took the church's bingo banner. It is now wrapped around the water tower.
So windy the Funeral Times arrived a page at a time, from three directions.
Gale-force gusts. A trash can rolls past, followed by its owner, followed by a dog.
Wind rattles the windows all day. You keep thinking someone is at the door.

weather.label: Black Ice
morning: Black ice on every road. Families who make it to your parlor are in no rush to leave.
The streets are glass. Your customers will stay for a second cup of coffee, and a third.
Treacherous roads. People take their time over everything, including grief.
Black ice. The hearse goes nowhere fast, and neither does anybody else.
Slick roads all morning. Mourners settle into your chairs like they live there.
Ice everywhere. The salt truck is in a ditch with its lights on.
Black ice. Two hearses slid into each other on Elm Street and the deceased swapped cars.
The roads are a skating rink. Visitors linger, and listen.

weather.label: Full Moon
morning: A full moon last night, and it's still hanging around. So are some very odd people.
The moon was full and red. Everybody who comes in today has a story.
Full moon. Old Man Withers was seen in the cornfield again, in the mask.
A big bright moon. The Reaper Club stayed open until it went down.
Full moon. Strange folk are about, and stranger deals.
The moon is full and Deacon howled at it all night. He says he's fine.
Full moon last night. Three people swore Morty waved at them.
A fat moon over the graveyard. Unusual customers are rattling your door knob.
weather.effect: more unusual customers and risky offers

weather.label: Smog (From Blaine)
morning: Smog drifting over from Blaine. Everyone is coughing and counting their change.
A brown haze from Blaine's crematorium. People are irritable and stingy.
Smog. The sun is a dim orange coin, and everybody's holding on to theirs.
Blaine's chimneys are at it again. Families come in wheezing and suspicious.
The air tastes like Blaine. Nobody is in a generous mood.
A yellow haze over town. Customers squint at your price list like it insulted them.
Smog so thick you could bottle it, and Blaine probably will.
Hazy and sour. The kind of day people ask what the cheapest option is, twice.

traits.label: Haggler
traits.hint: Wants a deal. Discounts calm them twice as much; a Hard Sell goes down badly.
lines: {customer}"Before we start, I never pay sticker price. Not for tires, not for {dHim}."
{customer}"What kind of discount do you do for cash? Or for no receipt?"
{customer}"Everything's negotiable. I once talked a cop down to a warning and a sandwich."
{customerName} circles the prices in the brochure and writes lower ones next to them.

traits.label: Guilt-Ridden Heir
traits.hint: Inherited everything and feels awful about it. Didn't love the deceased; Guilt works extra well.
lines: {customer}"{dHeCap} left me the house, the boat and the timeshare. I didn't even visit at Christmas."
{customer}"The will reading is Tuesday. I should feel sadder than I do."
{customer}"I got everything. My sister got the cat. She's not speaking to me. The cat is."

traits.label: In a Hurry
traits.hint: Has somewhere to be: little patience and no time for coffee.
lines: {customer}"I'm double parked, so whatever you're going to do, do it fast."
{customer}"I've got a thing at four. Another thing at four-fifteen. Let's move this along."
{customerName} hasn't taken {cHis} coat off, or {cHis} car keys out of {cHis} hand.

traits.label: Penny-Pincher
traits.hint: Hates spending money. Harder to sell, harder to read, and allergic to anything prestigious.
lines: {customer}"I brought my own coupons. They're for a pizza place but I think they should count."
{customer}"Do you charge for the chair I'm sitting in? Because I'll stand."
{customerName} has turned off the lamp on your desk. "You weren't using it."

traits.label: Show-Off
traits.hint: Wants the neighbors talking. Anything flashy sells itself.
lines: {customer}"The Hendersons had a horse-drawn carriage. I want two horses. Bigger horses."
{customer}"Money is no object. Well, it's an object. A shiny one I like to wave around."
{customer}"When people drive past the cemetery I want them to slow down and say 'whose is THAT?'"

traits.label: Heartbroken
traits.hint: Truly grieving. Loved the deceased; Sympathy works wonders, and Guilt is cruel.
lines: {customerName} can barely get the words out between sobs.
{customer}"We had plans. We had so many plans. Now it's just me and the parakeet."
{customerName} blows {cHis} nose, apologises, and starts crying again at the word "casket".

traits.label: Estranged
traits.hint: Hadn't spoken in years. Didn't love the deceased; Guilt works, sentimental extras fall flat.
lines: {customer}"Last time I saw {dHim} was 1987. {dHeCap} owed me twenty bucks."
{customer}"The hospital found my number in {dHis} phone under 'Do Not Answer'."
{customer}"I had to look at a photo to remember what {dHe} looked like. It was a mugshot."

traits.label: Skeptic
traits.hint: Thinks you are a crook. A Hard Sell bounces off, but they open up when you Listen.
lines: {customerName} reads every word of the price list, then reads it again upside down.
{customer}"I watched a documentary about you people."
{customer}"Before you say anything, I know what a casket costs to make. I looked it up."

traits.label: Devout
traits.hint: Church every Sunday. Loves religious touches; cremation is out of the question.
lines: {customer}"Father Smyth said you were... adequate."
{customerName} makes the sign of the cross every time you mention a price.
{customer}"{dFirst} is with the Lord now. I want the Lord to see {dHim} arrive in style."

traits.label: Hot-Headed
traits.hint: Short fuse: everything annoys them more, and coffee helps more.
lines: {customer}"The guy at the hospital looked at me funny. Don't look at me funny."
{customerName} has already kicked your umbrella stand.
{customer}"I'm calm. I'm CALM. Why does everybody keep asking if I'm calm?"

traits.label: Sentimental
traits.hint: Keeps everything. Keepsakes and flowers practically sell themselves.
lines: {customer}"I still have {dHis} baby teeth in a jar. Is that weird? Don't answer that."
{customerName} is clutching a shoebox of old photos and one sock.
{customer}"I kept the ticket stub from every movie we saw together. Can those go in with {dHim}?"

traits.label: Eco-Minded
traits.hint: Wants it natural. Open to cremation and green extras, appalled by embalming.
lines: {customer}"Is the casket compostable? {dHeCap} would want to be a tree. A small tree. A shrub."
{customerName} arrived on a bicycle with a trailer, looking for a place to plug it in.
{customer}"No chemicals. I don't want {dHim} pickled. I want {dHim} returned to the earth, like a banana peel."

traits.label: Here for the Buffet
traits.hint: Mostly here for the food. Catering sells easily; little else impresses them.
lines: {customer}"Is there a lunch after? There's usually a lunch after. I'd like to know about the lunch."
{customerName} keeps glancing at the candy dish on your desk, then at you, then at the candy dish.
{customer}"At Aunt Bev's funeral they had a ham shaped like Aunt Bev. That's the bar."

traits.label: Music Lover
traits.hint: Lives for music. Musical extras sell well, and they warm up to Sympathy.
lines: {customerName} is humming {dFirst}'s favorite song and tapping the rhythm on your desk.
{customer}"Whatever we do, the music has to be right. Bad music at a funeral is a second death."
{customer}"{dHeCap} sang in the shower every morning. Badly. I want something that sounds like that, but good."

traits.label: Chatterbox
traits.hint: Talks forever: a lot of patience, and every Listen reveals twice as much. Hard to read at a glance.
lines: {customer}"So anyway, before I get to {dFirst}, you have to understand about my sister's knee."
{customerName} has been talking for ten minutes and has not yet reached the part where someone died.
{customer}"Stop me if I've told you this. No, don't stop me. Where was I?"

traits.label: Tight-Lipped
traits.hint: Gives nothing away: a wide estimate and Sympathy falls flat, but endlessly patient.
lines: {customerName} answers every question with a nod, a shrug, or nothing.
{customer}"Don't need to talk about it. Just the funeral."
{customerName} sits very still and lets you do all the talking. It's unnerving.

traits.label: Bean Counter
traits.hint: Knows their budget to the cent and tells you: a narrow estimate. Stingy, and loves a Discount.
lines: {customer}"I've allocated a budget. I have it in a spreadsheet. The spreadsheet has tabs."
{customerName} asks for the price of everything to the cent, and writes it down in a ledger.
{customer}"I'd like an itemised quote, please, including tax and whatever you call the smell fee."

traits.label: Litigious
traits.hint: Threatens to sue over everything: quick to anger, Guilt half as useful, Hard Sells bounce.
lines: {customer}"I want you to know my lawyer is on speed dial. He's also my cousin. He's on speed dial twice."
{customer}"Is this conversation being recorded? Because I'm recording it."
{customerName} asks for your full name, spelled, "for the paperwork". There is no paperwork.

traits.label: Superstitious
traits.hint: Believes in omens and spirits. Spooky and religious extras work; cremation feels like bad luck.
lines: {customerName} throws salt over {cHis} shoulder before sitting down. Some of it hits you.
{customer}"A black cat crossed my path on the way here. Twice. It was the same cat. It went back for me."
{customer}"{dHeCap} broke a mirror in March. I said this would happen. Nobody listened."

traits.label: Death Enthusiast
traits.hint: Thinks death is the coolest thing that ever happened to anyone. Spooky extras sell; sentimental ones don't.
lines: {customer}"Is it true you drain the blood? Where does it go? Can I see where it goes?"
{customerName} is wearing black lipstick and a shirt that says I'D RATHER BE EMBALMED.
{customer}"I've always wanted to plan a funeral. I mean, I'm sorry about {dFirst}. But also, finally."

traits.label: Conspiracy Buff
traits.hint: Trusts nothing but locks and sealed boxes. Practical security extras sell; Listen gets twice the rambling truth.
lines: {customer}"Does the casket lock? From the outside? And who has the key? Write down who has the key."
{customer}"The coroner says {aFridge}. That's what they WANT us to think."
{customerName} checks under your desk for microphones, finds a gum wrapper, and pockets it as evidence.

traits.label: No-Nonsense
traits.hint: Wants it plain and useful. Practical extras sell; vanity and keepsakes don't. Short patience.
lines: {customer}"I don't need a dove release. I need a box, a hole and a lid that stays shut."
{customer}"Skip the poetry. What does it do, and what does it cost?"
{customerName} wipes your sales brochure off the desk with one sweep and says, "Next."

traits.label: Town Gossip
traits.hint: Cares what everyone will say. Guilt about appearances works, and prestige sells. Sticks around to chat.
lines: {customer}"Did you hear about the Pickett funeral? Paper plates. PAPER. At a FUNERAL."
{customerName} tells you three secrets about your competitors before you've even said hello.
{customer}"People are going to talk. I'm going to talk. I want to have something nice to talk about."

traits.label: Pushover
traits.hint: Agrees with everyone and calms down easily, but there isn't much money behind the smile.
lines: {customer}"Oh, whatever you think is best. You're the expert. Sorry. Sorry for saying sorry."
{customerName} apologises for coming in, for sitting down, and for {dFirst} dying on a weekday.
{customer}"I'm not good at saying no. My cousin has borrowed my car for six years."

traits.label: Insurance Payout
traits.hint: The check just cleared: a big budget, and they know exactly how big. Guilt works less; they feel entitled.
lines: {customer}"The insurance check cleared this morning. I counted it in the car. Twice. Then once more for fun."
{customer}"{dHeCap} was insured for a lot more than {dHe} was worth. I mean that with love. Some love."
{customerName} keeps patting {cHis} breast pocket, where something thick and envelope-shaped lives.

traits.label: Flat Broke
traits.hint: Not much money, and not afraid to say so. Small budget, but Sympathy goes a long way.
lines: {customer}"I'll be honest, I've got about four dollars and a really good attitude."
{customerName}'s coat is held together with safety pins and determination.
{customer}"I want to do right by {dHim}. I just need right to be on the cheaper side."

traits.label: Holds a Grudge
traits.hint: Never forgave the deceased. Doesn't love them, arrives angry, and coffee does little. Guilt bites hard.
lines: {customer}"{dHeCap} ran over my mailbox in 1992 and never apologised. I want that on the stone."
{customer}"I'm here to make sure {dHe}'s really dead. Then we'll talk about the box."
{customerName} spits the name "{dFirst}" like it tastes of something.

traits.label: Came Home Too Late
traits.hint: Loved the deceased and missed the end. Sympathy and keepsakes work; Guilt cuts deep.
lines: {customer}"I was going to visit this summer. I kept saying this summer."
{customerName} is still carrying a suitcase with an airline tag on it.
{customer}"The last thing I said to {dHim} was 'talk soon'. I want something that says sorry for that."

traits.label: Nervous Wreck
traits.hint: Jumpy and anxious: everything upsets them more and coffee barely helps (they're jittery enough), but Sympathy soothes.
lines: {customerName} jumps when your phone rings, then when it stops ringing.
{customer}"Is it hot in here? It's hot in here. Is it me? Is it the bodies? Are there bodies?"
{customerName} has shredded a tissue into confetti and started on a second one.

traits.label: Executor of the Estate
traits.hint: Spending someone else's money: a bigger budget and a cool head, but no love lost and no interest in discounts.
lines: {customer}"I'm the executor. The estate is paying. Just send the bill to the estate."
{customer}"The will says 'a dignified service'. I'm paid by the hour, so let's define dignified quickly."
{customerName} has a briefcase, a notarised letter and the warmth of a filing cabinet.

traits.label: Kitsch Collector
traits.hint: Loves anything weird and novel. Novelty extras sell like hotcakes; prestige leaves them cold.
lines: {customer}"Do you have anything with {dHis} face on it? A mug? A snow globe? A bobblehead?"
{customerName}'s keychain has nineteen tiny plastic things on it, and one key.
{customer}"The tackier the better. {dFirst} had a lamp shaped like a leg. I want that energy."

traits.label: Country Club
traits.hint: Old money and older manners. Big budget, prestige sells, and gold caskets go down easy; plain extras offend.
lines: {customer}"We're a Lake Bleak family. Lakefront. You understand."
{customerName} wipes the chair with a handkerchief before sitting on it.
{customer}"We don't do 'nice'. Nice is for Blaine. We do 'appropriate'."

traits.label: Germophobe
traits.hint: Terrified of germs. Embalming and practical sealed extras sell; cremation sounds hygienic.
lines: {customerName} won't shake your hand. Or touch the pen. Or look at the chair.
{customer}"Is the body... clean? Like, clean clean? Hospital clean? Cleaner than hospital?"
{customerName} wipes down your desk with {cHis} own wet wipes, then wipes down the wet wipes.

traits.label: Sibling Rivalry
traits.hint: Spending to outdo the rest of the family. Guilt about what the relatives will think works; Sympathy doesn't.
lines: {customer}"My brother is going to see this funeral. I want him to see it and feel small."
{customer}"Whatever my sister would pick, I want the next one up."
{customerName} takes a photo of the price list "for evidence".

traits.label: Animal Lover
traits.hint: Cares more about animals than people. Green extras and sentimental touches work; Sympathy helps.
lines: {customerName} has dog hair on every inch of {cHis} clothes and is proud of every hair.
{customer}"Is there a pet section? {dHeCap} would want to be near the dogs. Honestly, so would I."
{customer}"Did they say how the cat's taking it? Someone needs to tell the cat."

traits.label: Funeral Veteran
traits.hint: Has buried half the family and knows the tricks. Hard Sells bounce, but they respect a Discount.
lines: {customer}"This is my fourth funeral this year. I've got a punch card from the florist."
{customer}"Don't do the speech about worms. I've heard the speech about worms."
{customerName} corrects you on the price of a plot, accurately, from memory.

traits.label: Serene
traits.hint: Calm as a pond: arrives relaxed and hardly gets angry, but Guilt and Sympathy barely move them.
lines: {customerName} breathes in slowly through {cHis} nose and smiles at nothing in particular.
{customer}"Death is just a door. I'm here to pick the door."
{customerName} hasn't blinked in a while and seems perfectly at peace with your prices.

traits.label: Shutterbug
traits.hint: Photographing everything for later. Looks matter: flowers and vanity extras sell; patience is short.
lines: {customerName} takes a photo of the casket, then of you, then of you with the casket.
{customer}"Is the lighting in the viewing room good? I want the pictures to come out."
{customer}"Can we do {dHis} hair like in this photo? Not this one. This one. Scroll back."

traits.label: Know-It-All
traits.hint: Has read up and brags about it, including what they can spend: a narrow estimate. Hard to guilt, quick to scoff.
lines: {customer}"Actually, embalming isn't legally required. I read that. I read a lot."
{customer}"I've budgeted exactly what the industry average is, plus four percent for emotional damages."
{customerName} explains your own job to you, wrongly, for several minutes.

traits.label: Spiritual Seeker
traits.hint: Crystals and auras. Spooky and green extras appeal; church stuff and embalming don't.
lines: {customer}"{dFirst}'s aura was a sort of mustard color at the end. I want something to balance that."
{customerName} places a crystal on your desk "to absorb your energy". It's not clear whose side it's on.
{customer}"We're not saying goodbye. We're saying 'see you on the next plane'. The astral one."

traits.label: Traditionalist
traits.hint: Wants it the way it's always been done. Religious touches and embalming sell; cremation and novelties don't.
lines: {customer}"Black hearse, black suits, an organ, a hole. That's a funeral. Anything else is a party."
{customer}"My grandfather was buried properly, and his grandfather. I'm not breaking the chain for {dFirst}."
{customerName} frowns at the word "celebration" in your brochure and crosses it out.

traits.label: Secretly Relieved
traits.hint: Didn't love the deceased and is quietly glad. Arrives calm; keepsakes fall flat; a little Guilt goes a long way.
lines: {customerName} looks ten years younger than {cHe} probably did last week.
{customer}"It's very sad. Very, very sad. I slept nine hours last night."
{customer}"{dHeCap} was a difficult person. It's going to be so quiet. So nice and quiet."

traits.label: Loudmouth
traits.hint: Says everything at full volume. Loves loud music; a bit touchy, but sticks around.
lines: {customer}"I SAID WE'RE HERE ABOUT {dFirst}! NO, I'M NOT SHOUTING!"
{customerName} laughs at something you said so loudly that a mourner in the next room drops a cup.
{customer}"I want a BAND. And a horn section. {dFirst} wasn't a quiet person and this won't be a quiet funeral!"

traits.label: Minimalist
traits.hint: Owns six things and wants it simple. Vanity and prestige extras flop; green ones are welcome.
lines: {customer}"Just the essentials. {dFirst} owned one fork. One. {dHeCap} was happy."
{customerName} looks at the gold-trim brochure like it insulted {cHis} mother.
{customer}"Less is more. Except the price. Less price is less."

paint.name: Fresh Paint
paint.description: Covers the graffiti and most of the smell. Your first step out of the shack.

coffee-machine.name: Coffee Machine
coffee-machine.description: Real coffee instead of the jar of brown dust. Offer Coffee calms customers half again as much.

guard-dog.name: Guard Dog
guard-dog.description: Security level 1: rivals sometimes get chased off at the door, and you hit harder in a fight at home. Eats like three dogs.

florist-cooler.name: Florist Cooler
florist-cooler.description: Unlocks the top flower tiers (Wall of Lilies and up). Also keeps the lemonade cold.

storeroom.name: Storeroom
storeroom.description: Room for 18 caskets instead of 6. Elijah's 64-year-old boy hates you already.

embalming-lab.name: Embalming Lab
embalming-lab.description: Unlocks Air-Brushed Embalming and Museum-Grade Preservation. The fumes are only mildly illegal.

alarm.name: Alarm System
alarm.description: Security level 2. Needs the Guard Dog, who howls along every time it goes off.

viewing-room.name: Viewing Room
viewing-room.description: Somewhere to sit that isn't a casket. Customers have 2 more patience. Needs Fresh Paint.

incinerator.name: Incinerator
incinerator.description: Unlocks the cremation track: offer to cremate instead of bury, then sell urns. Do not use it for the leaves.

night-watchman.name: Night Watchman
night-watchman.description: Security level 3. He is mostly asleep, but loudly, and families like a parlor with a man at the door: richer families notice you. Needs the Alarm System.

chapel.name: Chapel
chapel.description: A real chapel. Richer families come to you, and the full-orchestra service opens up. Needs the Viewing Room.

mausoleum.name: Mausoleum
mausoleum.description: Marble everything. Unlocks the crypt plots, which pay well every day. Needs the Chapel.

billboard.name: Billboard on Route 9
billboard.description: Your face, forty feet wide, next to the words YOU'RE NEXT. Richer families notice you. Needs a signage permit from City Hall.

memorial-garden.name: Memorial Garden
memorial-garden.description: Roses, a fountain, a bench nobody sits on. Customers have 2 more patience, and richer families notice you. Needs a zoning permit from City Hall.

crematorium.name: Crematorium
crematorium.description: A real crematorium with a chimney you can see from Blaine. Richer families notice you. Needs the Incinerator and a crematory permit from City Hall.
